In addition to the raksha's normal shaping action, this Charm lets her make one Sword-shaping or Staff-shaping attack for each 3 motes of Essence spent, up to a limit of her permanent Essence.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 197 (PDF 198). Capstone of the God-Humbling Victory Sword / Pincer of Transcendent Time and Fate line.

name: Host-Summoning Glory of Command
summary: The second independent root of the Sword Combat Charms tree: the raksha wears a visible mantle of martial greatness, letting her draw armies, monsters and champions into an ongoing story and instantly ready a Sword- or Staff-shaping weapon before her initiative.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 1; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha wears the mantle of greatness, visibly displaying her terrible aptitude for war. She can draw her armies, monsters and champions into an ongoing story without further explanation of their presence. This Charm instantly readies a Sword-shaping or Staff-shaping weapon; the raksha can use this Charm before her initiative.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 197 (PDF 198). Second of two independent roots of the diagrammed 'Sword Combat Charms 1' tree.

name: Sundering the Gates of Death
summary: Lets the raksha instantly re-ready a slain or scattered Sword- or Staff-shaping weapon (army, behemoth or even her own body) before her initiative, though it cannot restore the permanently slain.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: Host-Summoning Glory of Command.
mechanics: The raksha commands death, and it is not her master. If her army is slain or scattered, she can call it back; if her behemoth is slain or driven away, she can restore it; even should an enemy shatter her bones and leave her bloody and broken on the field, she can restore herself and continue the fight. This Charm instantly readies a Sword-shaping or Staff-shaping weapon, even if that weapon has been slain or otherwise driven from the battle; the raksha can use it before her initiative. This Charm cannot restore the permanently slain.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 197 (PDF 198). Also feeds forward as a co-prerequisite (alongside Radiance of the Invincible Warrior) of Rarefied Air of Inevitable Victory in the 'Sword Combat Charms 2' tree below -- a cross-tree convergence confirmed in the rendered diagram, where this Charm's box reappears in both trees.

name: Transient Work of Flesh and Bone
summary: Shapes a behemoth or a host of warriors out of gossamer as a Sword-shaping weapon, built from the raksha's own Sword Grace and Willpower, though the work of glamour cannot affect Creation-born residents above a Wits + Essence threshold.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 3; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Host-Summoning Glory of Command.
mechanics: The raksha shapes a behemoth or a host of warriors from gossamer. This Charm forms a shaping weapon of the Sword; the player divides twice the raksha's Sword Grace between the weapon's speed, accuracy, damage and defense, and its rate equals the raksha's permanent Willpower. The weapon formed is a monster (a fey beast) or a small army (a unit of 500 extras using the elite troop Traits from Exalted core, p. 278). Either way the result is a work of glamour: it cannot attack, defend or soak against residents of Creation whose Wits + Essence exceeds the raksha's Valor.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 197 (PDF 198, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 199). Also feeds forward as a co-prerequisite (alongside World-Devouring Warlord Stance) of Gathering the Crows in the 'World-Devouring Warlord Style' sub-tree below -- another cross-tree convergence confirmed in the rendered diagram.

name: Scattering the Foe
summary: The root of two further Sword Combat Charm branches: takes on the aspect of Shikhari, the hammer that scatters armies, letting the raksha buy dice to block a Sword- or Staff-shaping attack even from nothing, provided she is aware of it.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 1; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha's sword takes on the aspect of Shikhari, the hammer that scatters armies. An enemy attack shatters against the raksha's battle prowess. This Charm allows the raksha to buy dice for blocking Sword or Staff attacks -- she can improve a normal shaping parry or build a shaping dice pool from nothing. She must be aware of the attack.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 197 (PDF 198). Root of both the diagrammed 'Sword Combat Charms 2' tree (via Radiance of the Invincible Warrior) and 'Sword Combat Charms 3' tree (via All-Inclusive Nightmare Defense); its box reappears in both diagrams.

name: Radiance of the Invincible Warrior
summary: Binds back fear and death from the raksha's assembled forces, letting her parry any one Sword or Staff attack with her full dice pool provided she is aware of it.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: Scattering the Foe.
mechanics: The raksha's Sword Grace binds back fear and death, so that they come only grudgingly to her assembled forces. This Charm lets the raksha parry any one Sword or Staff attack with her full dice pool. She must be aware of the attack.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 197 (PDF 198, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 199). Root of the diagrammed 'Sword Combat Charms 2' tree.

name: Waypoint-Sealing Technique
summary: Takes up the Raghava aspect of the Sword's defensive posture, letting the raksha seal an opponent out of a waypoint she occupies or controls with an undodgeable Sword-shaping attack.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 3; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: Radiance of the Invincible Warrior.
mechanics: Taking up the powerful defensive position typified by the Raghava aspect of the Sword, the raksha seals an opponent out of a waypoint. The raksha uses this Charm as an opponent enters a waypoint she occupies or controls, and her player rolls Dexterity + Melee as an undodgeable Sword-shaping attack. If she achieves even one success, the opponent cannot enter the waypoint this scene and loses that portion of her movement.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 198 (PDF 199). The diagrammed 'Sword Combat Charms 2' tree box labels this Charm 'Waypoint Sealing Stance,' but its own header and stat block both read 'Waypoint-Sealing Technique' with Type: Reflexive (not a Stance-type Charm); flagged as a diagram/header naming mismatch following this inventory's established precedent (e.g. swift-wings-of-song, impinging-web-of-dream).

name: Unconquerable Truth
summary: Invokes truths of the raksha that no weaving of fate can master, letting her parry any one Sword- or Staff-shaping attack with her full dice pool plus six bonus successes, even against a normally unblockable attack.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 4; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Radiance of the Invincible Warrior.
mechanics: There are some warriors who cannot be defeated; there are some generals whom no mind can outmaneuver; there are truths of the raksha that no paltry weaving of fate and story can master. This Charm lets the raksha parry any one Sword- or Staff-shaping attack with her full dice pool, adding six bonus successes, even if that attack is normally unblockable.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 198 (PDF 199).

name: Rarefied Air of Inevitable Victory
summary: The raksha masters the destiny of war for a full story, reflexively parrying any Sword or Staff attack against her with her full dice pool even without being aware of it.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 5; Minimum Essence: 3; Prerequisite Charms: Sundering the Gates of Death, Radiance of the Invincible Warrior.
mechanics: The raksha masters the destiny of war. Cast itself at her though it might, the enemy cannot keep her forces down -- they endure the most horrific assaults, they regroup after the most terrible of blows, and not all the greatest nightmares of the Wyld can keep the raksha from her appointed goal. This Charm allows the raksha to reflexively parry any Sword or Staff attack against her with her full dice pool; she need not be aware of the attack. This paramount skill lasts until the end of the story.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 198 (PDF 199). Cross-tree convergence Charm: combines the 'Sword Combat Charms 1' tree's Sundering the Gates of Death with the 'Sword Combat Charms 2' tree's own root line (Radiance of the Invincible Warrior), confirmed in the rendered diagram.

name: Defining the Parameters of Battle
summary: Writes the raksha's own invincibility into the pattern of the world for a full story, letting her spend gossamer to parry any Sword-, Staff-, or even mortal attack with her full dice pool plus six bonus successes.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 5; Minimum Essence: 4; Prerequisite Charms: Unconquerable Truth, Rarefied Air of Inevitable Victory.
mechanics: The raksha writes her own invincibility into the pattern of the world. While this glamour endures, no Sword shaping can defy the essential truths of her nature: she can spend 1 gossamer to parry any one Sword- or Staff-shaping attack with her full dice pool plus six bonus successes, even if that attack is normally unblockable. In addition, she can spend 1 gossamer to parry any mortal attack with her full Dexterity + Melee pool plus six bonus successes, even if normally unblockable; this defense is a work of glamour and does not function against mortals with Wits + Essence greater than the raksha's Stamina.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 198 (PDF 199, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 200). Capstone of the diagrammed 'Sword Combat Charms 2' tree.

name: All-Inclusive Nightmare Defense
summary: Unleashes fear and doubt on the raksha's enemies after a successful parry, disarming the attacker's Sword- or Staff-shaping weapon from readiness by routing or killing the forces behind it.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Scattering the Foe.
mechanics: The raksha unleashes fear and doubt upon her enemies, dispersing and driving back the weapons of the Sword. To use this Charm, she must successfully parry a Sword attack and receive extra successes equal to or exceeding the attacker's permanent Essence. This Charm removes the enemy's Sword-shaping or Staff-shaping weapon from readiness, normally by routing or killing the enemy's forces.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 199 (PDF 200). Root of the diagrammed 'Sword Combat Charms 3' tree, the second branch off Scattering the Foe.

name: Tension-Building Warrior's Advance
summary: Takes on the aspect of the supreme divine emissary of death, supplementing a Sword or Staff attack by raising the difficulty of all shaping parries against it and, on success, stripping the enemy's shaping weapon from readiness; cannot be used for surprise attacks.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: All-Inclusive Nightmare Defense.
mechanics: The footsteps of the raksha ring loudly in the air. He takes on the aspect of the supreme divine emissary of death; as nothing can stand against him, nothing will. This Charm supplements a Sword or Staff attack, adding the raksha's Essence to the difficulty of all shaping parries against it. If the attack succeeds, the Charm also removes the enemy's shaping weapon from readiness. This Charm cannot be used for surprise attacks.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 199 (PDF 200, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 201).

name: Fearsome Mien
summary: A work of glamour that weaves a terrifying aura after a successful Sword attack, imposing a two-die dice-pool penalty on all Creation-born enemies interacting with the raksha for a scene.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 3; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Tension-Building Warrior's Advance.
mechanics: The raksha can weave a glamour that terrifies creatures of Creation. This requires a successful Sword attack. This Charm imposes a two-die penalty to the dice pools of all Creation-born enemies interacting with the character. This is a work of glamour, and it has no effect on creatures with Valor + Essence greater than the raksha's highest Sword Ability (Archery, Athletics, Brawl, Melee or Presence).
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' section, p. 199 (PDF 200, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 201). Capstone of the diagrammed 'Sword Combat Charms 3' tree.

name: Aegis of a Martial Destiny
summary: The root Charm of World-Devouring Warlord Style, a named sub-tree of Sword Combat Charms telling the story of an emissary of death and fear who rises to cast the world into his shadow: establishes the raksha's motivation for battle early in the story, augmenting a shaping Dodge action with automatic successes equal to her Sword.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 1; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Early in the story, the raksha establishes her motivation for battle. She cannot use this Charm if she has taken an aggressive shaping action this story. The raksha uses this Charm to augment a shaping Dodge action; this Charm adds her Sword in automatic successes to her Dodge roll.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' -> 'World-Devouring Warlord Style' sub-tree, p. 200 (PDF 201). Root of this named style's own diagram, distinct from (but following the same 'named sub-style within a Charm section' pattern as) Laughing Monster Style in the Staff Grace tree and Spirit-Twisting Obsession Style in the Cup Grace tree.

name: Antagonist-Naming Technique
summary: Defines the raksha and a chosen (existing) antagonist as the principal characters of the story, preventing shaping actions that would remove either of them as active characters -- for example, killing the raksha would have to somehow also bring her back to life.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: Aegis of a Martial Destiny.
mechanics: The raksha defines herself and an antagonist of her choice as the principal characters of the story; the antagonist must exist. This Charm prevents the use of shaping actions that remove the raksha or her named antagonist as active characters in the story. For example, no one can use a shaping action to kill the raksha without also in some fashion bringing her back to life.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' -> 'World-Devouring Warlord Style' sub-tree, p. 200 (PDF 201).

name: Thematic Stunting Methodology
summary: Defines desirable premises of the story and genre for a full story, adding five extra dice to the raksha's stunt pool.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: Aegis of a Martial Destiny.
mechanics: The raksha defines desirable premises of the story and genre. This adds five extra dice to her stunt pool.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' -> 'World-Devouring Warlord Style' sub-tree, p. 200 (PDF 201). Second branch off Aegis of a Martial Destiny, parallel to Antagonist-Naming Technique.

name: World-Devouring Warlord Stance
summary: A Stance-type Charm pouring Essence into the raksha's Sword Grace, adding her permanent Essence to initiative, Sword attack pools, Sword defense pools, and the raw pre-soak damage of Sword attacks; only one Stance-type Charm can be active at a time.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 3; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Antagonist-Naming Technique, Thematic Stunting Methodology.
mechanics: The raksha pours Essence into her Sword Grace. Flush with the power of the Sword, she becomes a devotee of battle and assumes the stance of an all-devouring warlord. This Charm adds the raksha's permanent Essence to her initiative, her Sword attack pools, her Sword defense pools, and the raw (pre-soak) damage of Sword attacks. This is a Stance-type Charm; characters cannot use more than one Stance-type Charm at a time.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' -> 'World-Devouring Warlord Style' sub-tree, p. 200 (PDF 201). Central convergence node of the style's diagram, feeding Gathering the Crows, Army-Supporting Behemoth Invocation and Harmony of Fortune and Hate below.

name: Gathering the Crows
summary: Summons a greater host of literal-extra troops to swell the raksha's army, cumulatively increasing the defense quality of her chosen shaping weapon by one per invocation.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 4; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Transient Work of Flesh and Bone, World-Devouring Warlord Stance.
mechanics: The raksha summons servants and minions. Each invocation of this Charm calls forth a greater host to support her in war. Most of the troops are literal extras -- they don't ever interact with enemies directly, but they swell the raksha's army ominously. This Charm increases the defense quality of her chosen shaping weapon by one, and multiple invocations of this Charm are cumulative.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' -> 'World-Devouring Warlord Style' sub-tree, p. 200 (PDF 201, with the Prerequisite Charms line and mechanics text continuing onto PDF 202). Cross-tree convergence Charm: combines this style's own World-Devouring Warlord Stance with the earlier 'Sword Combat Charms 1' tree's Transient Work of Flesh and Bone, confirmed in the rendered diagram.

name: Army-Supporting Behemoth Invocation
summary: Summons monsters, horrors and war machines to support the raksha's army, cumulatively increasing the damage of her chosen shaping weapon by one per invocation.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 4; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: World-Devouring Warlord Stance.
mechanics: The raksha summons monsters, horrors and war machines to serve with his army. Each use of this Charm supports his forces with another great monster or a handful of smaller beasts. This Charm increases the damage of her chosen shaping weapon by one, and multiple invocations of this Charm are cumulative.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' -> 'World-Devouring Warlord Style' sub-tree, p. 201 (PDF 202). Parallel to Gathering the Crows, both branching off World-Devouring Warlord Stance and converging on Avatar of War.

name: Avatar of War
summary: Closing her ears to screams and blandishments alike, the raksha marches to war: an immediate full-dice-pool Sword counterattack against any character attacking her with a shaping action, resolved before the original attack's damage is determined.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 4; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Gathering the Crows, Army-Supporting Behemoth Invocation.
mechanics: Closing her ears to screams and blandishments alike, the raksha marches to war. This Charm lets her immediately execute a Sword attack at her full dice pool against any character attacking her with a shaping action. This counterattack is resolved after the original attack is rolled but before its damage is determined.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' -> 'World-Devouring Warlord Style' sub-tree, p. 201 (PDF 202). Converges Gathering the Crows and Army-Supporting Behemoth Invocation; feeds forward into Preemptive Declaration of Victory alongside Harmony of Fortune and Hate.

name: Harmony of Fortune and Hate
summary: Bends hostile weather, ill fortune and unpleasant terrain against the enemy's will to fight, cumulatively increasing the difficulty of defending against the raksha's Sword attacks (up to a maximum equal to her Essence).
requirements: Minimum Sword: 4; Minimum Essence: 3; Prerequisite Charms: World-Devouring Warlord Stance.
mechanics: The pattern of events develops inexorably in the raksha's favor. Hostile weather, strokes of ill fortune and unpleasant terrain eat away at the enemy's will and power to fight. Each use of this Charm increases the difficulty of defense against the raksha's Sword attacks by one; multiple invocations of this Charm stack, up to a maximum increased difficulty equal to the raksha's Essence.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' -> 'World-Devouring Warlord Style' sub-tree, p. 201 (PDF 202, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 203). Third branch off World-Devouring Warlord Stance, alongside Gathering the Crows and Army-Supporting Behemoth Invocation; feeds forward into Preemptive Declaration of Victory alongside Avatar of War.

name: Preemptive Declaration of Victory
summary: The capstone of World-Devouring Warlord Style: a Sword attack that converts damage dice directly into successes and, on success, forces all shaped creatures in combat with the raksha to succeed at a Valor roll or surrender in a five-die-penalized rout for the rest of the scene.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 5; Minimum Essence: 3; Prerequisite Charms: Avatar of War, Harmony of Fortune and Hate.
mechanics: Crushing her enemy underfoot, the raksha declares victory. The raksha makes a Sword attack; if she succeeds, this Charm converts the damage dice directly into successes. The damage of this attack can affect the creatures of Creation: if the Sword attack succeeds, all shaped creatures directly or indirectly in combat with the character realize themselves defeated, and their players must succeed at a Valor roll or the characters lay down their arms in resigned surrender. For the rest of the scene, the defeated suffer a five-die penalty on all combat actions. This Charm is a work of glamour and has no effect on creatures with Valor + Essence greater than the raksha's highest Sword Ability (Archery, Athletics, Brawl, Melee or Presence).
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Sword Combat Charms' -> 'World-Devouring Warlord Style' sub-tree, p. 202 (PDF 203). Capstone of the diagrammed World-Devouring Warlord Style tree and the last Charm of the entire Sword Combat Charms section. Its own header appears immediately before the 'MUTATION CHARMS' section header on the same page, marking the section boundary.

name: Pox
summary: A repeatable Charm of Shape that manifests a Wyld pox of the player's choice (per the pox lists in Exalted core or Exalted: The Lunars), useful in the design of behemoths.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 1; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha manifests a Wyld pox (see Exalted core, p. 280, or Exalted: The Lunars, p. 212) chosen at the time of the Charm's purchase. Players can purchase this Charm more than once, choosing a new pox each time.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 202 (PDF 203). This section's Charms are individually purchasable Charms of Shape (nearly all 'Prerequisite Charms: None') rather than a branching combat tree, unlike every other named Charm section in this Grace tree. Named after the mutation categories (pox/affliction/blight) rather than describing the mechanical effect, which is a fixed table entry chosen by the player at purchase and defined elsewhere in the core book / Exalted: The Lunars rather than in this book -- flagged here rather than transcribed, since this inventory covers Exalted: The Fair Folk only. `id` distinguished from a generic 'pox' to avoid collision with any future cross-splat mutation-table row.

name: Affliction
summary: A repeatable Charm of Shape that manifests a Wyld affliction of the player's choice (per the affliction lists in Exalted core or Exalted: The Lunars).
requirements: Minimum Sword: 1; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha manifests a Wyld affliction (see Exalted core, p. 280, or Exalted: The Lunars, pp. 212-215) chosen at the time of the Charm's purchase. Players can purchase this Charm more than once, choosing a new affliction each time.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 202 (PDF 203, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 204). `id` distinguished from a generic 'affliction' to avoid collision with any future cross-splat mutation-table row.

name: Blight
summary: A repeatable Charm of Shape that manifests a Wyld blight of the player's choice (per the blight lists in Exalted core or Exalted: The Lunars).
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha manifests a Wyld blight (see Exalted core, pp. 280-281, or Exalted: The Lunars, pp. 215-218) chosen at the time of the Charm's purchase. Players can purchase this Charm more than once, choosing a new blight each time.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 203 (PDF 204). `id` distinguished from a generic 'blight' to avoid collision with any future cross-splat mutation-table row.

name: Hundred-Hand Style
summary: Attunes the raksha's shape to the harmony of principles so mind and body function as many rather than one, reducing multiple-action penalties by 1 (to a minimum of 0).
requirements: Minimum Sword: 1; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha attunes her shape to the harmony of principles, so that her mind and body function as many rather than one. This Charm is favored by raksha with extra arms, heads or personalities, but these things are not necessary to receive the Charm's primary benefit. Activating this Charm reduces multiple action penalties by 1, to a minimum of 0.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 203 (PDF 204). Root of the small linear line Hundred-Hand Style -> Millipede Mind -> Grace of the Infinite Revolving Spheres / Harmonious Primordial Spirit, the only Charms in this section with a stated prerequisite other than None.

name: Millipede Mind
summary: Divides control of the raksha's mind and body among her five Graces, reducing multiple-action penalties by 2 (to a minimum of 0); stacks with its own prerequisite, Hundred-Hand Style.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Hundred-Hand Style.
mechanics: The raksha divides control of her mind and body among her Graces, so that five distinct principles guide her every action. Activating this Charm reduces multiple action penalties by 2, to a minimum of 0. The raksha can benefit from this Charm and its prerequisite simultaneously.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 203 (PDF 204). Stacks explicitly with Hundred-Hand Style rather than superseding it, an unusual stated exception to the game's normal non-stacking assumption.

name: Grace of the Infinite Revolving Spheres
summary: Lets the raksha flow through the interwoven desires of her five component Graces so that, when splitting her dice pool, her first five actions suffer no multiple-action penalties; stacks with its prerequisites.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 3; Prerequisite Charms: Millipede Mind.
mechanics: The raksha flows smoothly through the interwoven desires of his five component Graces. If he splits his dice pool, the first five actions suffer no multiple-action penalties. The raksha can benefit from this Charm and its prerequisites simultaneously.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 203 (PDF 204). Capstone of the Hundred-Hand Style -> Millipede Mind line; stacks explicitly with both prerequisites.

name: Harmonious Primordial Spirit
summary: Embeds one of the raksha's own Graces in a consenting common raksha, turning it into a bound spiritual-extension servant with heroic-commoner qualities that shares use of the embedded Grace with the original owner.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 4; Minimum Essence: 3; Prerequisite Charms: Millipede Mind.
mechanics: The raksha embeds one of her Graces in a consenting common raksha, replacing his own version of that Grace. The creature becomes a bound subsidiary entity, a spiritual extension of the raksha's body, with the qualities and abilities of a heroic commoner. The servant serves the raksha loyally and at all times knows her will. The activating raksha still has access to the Grace while this Charm is in effect, and the subsidiary raksha also uses this Grace for Charms and damage.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 203 (PDF 204, with the mechanics description on PDF 204/printed 203's second column). Second branch off Millipede Mind, parallel to Grace of the Infinite Revolving Spheres.

name: Long-Arm Technique
summary: Lets the raksha's limbs unfold like flowing geysers of flesh on attack, extending her reach by two yards per gossamer spent and letting her strike mounted opponents without penalty.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 1; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Raksha with this Charm are never quite so far from their victims as they might appear. Fair Folk under this Charm's influence look normal until they attack, when their limbs stretch and unfold like flowing geysers of flesh. For each gossamer spent, this Charm adds two yards to the raksha's reach. Raksha with this Charm active can strike opponents on horseback without penalty.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 203 (PDF 204).

name: Gossamer Wing Flight
summary: Shapes wings from mixed Wyld and Creation substance, letting the raksha fly at normal speed (half speed to ascend, double to dive), though the wings impose a Dexterity penalty while airborne unless the Charm is purchased a second time.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 1; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha forms wings for himself, shaping them from the mixed substances of the Wyld and Creation. Nobles often build their wings from the appropriate element; commoners base theirs on the wings of birds or insects. The raksha's wingspan is at least equal to his height, and he cannot fly if he cannot spread his wings; he can fly at normal speed, ascend at half speed, or dive at twice his normal speed. Gossamer wings are clumsy, and the character suffers a +2 difficulty penalty on all Dexterity-based normal dice actions while airborne; the player can eliminate this penalty by purchasing this Charm a second time. Raksha using either version of this Charm may make fly-by attacks (see the Exalted Players Guide, p. 201).
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 203 (PDF 204, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 205). Purchasable a second time to remove its own penalty, similar in structure to other doubly-purchasable Charms elsewhere in this inventory.

name: Hiding the Wyld's Touch
summary: Makes the raksha's body language and manner unnaturally human and familiar, granting two automatic successes on normal Social dice actions, though it does not hide an inhuman appearance -- it only makes others notice the 'person within.'
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha's body language and manner of expression are unnaturally human and familiar -- the monster moves and speaks like an amalgam of old friends, family and lovers. This Charm gives two automatic successes on normal Social dice actions. If the raksha is also hideously inhuman in appearance or behavior, this Charm does not force others to disregard this fact -- they simply find themselves noticing the 'person within.'
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 204 (PDF 205).

name: Armament of Flesh
summary: A permanent mutation granting understated but potent natural weaponry (fangs, nails or horns) sharp enough to puncture steel, usable with the raksha's normal Brawl or Martial Arts dice pools.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 1; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha develops understated but potent natural weaponry. Her small fangs, pointed nails or thin elegant horns are sharp enough to puncture steel. This affliction gives the raksha a natural attack with Speed -3, Accuracy +1, Defense -1, Damage +4L and Rate 4; she can use this attack with her normal Brawl or Martial Arts attack dice pools. The raksha can shape more blatant and obvious weaponry if desired -- subtlety is simply the standard.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 204 (PDF 205). Unlike most of this section's Charms, this and the remaining entries (Surpassing Excellence, Glorious Hero Form, Racing Dragon Speed, Root of the Perfected Lotus) are purchased with mutation points rather than motes, and are Type: Special / Duration: Permanent rather than the section's usual Reflexive/One-story pattern.

name: Surpassing Excellence
summary: A permanent mutation adding a two-die specialty (not counted against the raksha's specialty limit) to any one Ability, purchasable up to once per dot of the raksha's Sword.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 1; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: In a place between worlds, the raksha forges herself like a weapon, using the elemental Essence of Creation to empower one of her Abilities. This pox adds a permanent two-die specialty to any one Ability, which does not count against her specialty limit. Raksha can use this Charm to purchase inhumanly keen senses -- for example, a two-die Keen Eyesight specialty on Awareness gives benefits commensurate with the Eye Color pox (see Exalted core, p. 280, or Exalted: The Lunars, p. 212). Players can purchase this Charm up to once per dot of the raksha's Sword.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 204 (PDF 205).

name: Glorious Hero Form
summary: A permanent mutation binding the raksha to Caturbhuja, the shinma that breaks the borders of the possible and impossible, permanently raising a chosen pair (or single) of Attributes; purchasable up to once per dot of the raksha's Sword.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha binds herself to the principle Caturbhuja, the shinma that breaks the borders of the possible and impossible; she transcends even the perfection of the raksha. This affliction permanently increases her Attributes in one of the following ways (chosen at purchase): one dot of Strength and one dot of Stamina; one dot of Intelligence and one dot of Perception; one dot of Charisma and one dot of Appearance; one dot of Dexterity; one dot of Wits; or one dot of Manipulation. Players can purchase this Charm up to once per dot of the raksha's Sword.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 205 (PDF 206). This is the highest-value permanent Attribute-boosting mutation in the book relative to the earlier note on Attribute caps requiring Charm-granted mutations (e.g. Huge, Glorious Hero Form itself) to exceed 7 dots in a single Attribute.

name: Racing Dragon Speed
summary: A permanent mutation imbuing the raksha's body with the speed of wind, fire or waves, adding five yards to running speed; unusually purchasable up to once per dot of the raksha's Compassion rather than her Sword.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 1; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha imbues her body with the speed of the wind, the fire or the waves. This Charm permanently adds five yards to the raksha's running speed. Players can purchase this Charm up to once per dot of the raksha's Compassion.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 205 (PDF 206). Confirmed against the rendered page image that the repurchase cap really is keyed to Compassion, not Sword or Valor as every other repurchasable Charm in this section is -- flagged here since it is otherwise an outlier in a Sword-Grace Charm list.

name: Root of the Perfected Lotus
summary: A permanent mutation that sinks the raksha into the flows of Creation's Essence, granting her the destiny, spirit and attitude to learn Martial Arts Charms as a Dragon-Blooded.
requirements: Minimum Sword: 2; Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha sinks into the flows of the Essence of Creation, shaping in herself the destiny, spirit and attitude necessary to practice supernatural martial arts. This allows her to learn Martial Arts Charms as a Dragon-Blooded.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nishkriya, the Sword' -> 'Mutation Charms' section, p. 205 (PDF 206). Last Charm of the Mutation Charms section and of the entire Sword Grace tree (shinma Nishkriya); the 'GLAMOUR SORCERY' section header begins immediately afterward on the same page, marking both the section and the Chapter Five per-Grace-Charm-tree system's boundary -- with this Charm's completion, all five of Chapter Five's per-Grace Charm trees (Heart, Staff, Cup, Ring, Sword) are now fully inventoried.

name: Assumption of Elemental Shape
summary: The most common gateway Assumption-type Charm: lets a raksha pass through the shinma Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature within Creation, in one of five elemental variants (Air/Earth/Fire/Water/Wood) each granting a distinct minor elemental resistance or sense.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: This Charm allows a raksha to pass through the gateway Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature within Creation. This Charm is actually five different Charms, each offering a different benefit: Assumption of Elemental Shape (Air) -- the raksha suffers no ill effects from cold and may walk on snow or ice as if it were solid, stable ground; (Earth) -- the raksha can see clearly in the deepest darkness; (Fire) -- the raksha suffers no ill effects from heat or non-magical flame; (Water) -- the raksha can swim at normal movement rates, breathe water as well as air, and otherwise exist comfortably in an aquatic environment; (Wood) -- the raksha can balance on even the thinnest branch and entirely ignores any natural poison with a single success on a Stamina + Resistance roll. This is an Assumption-type Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Assumption-Type Charms' section, p. 149 (PDF 150). Root of the diagrammed 'Assumption Charms 1' and 'Assumption Charms 2' trees. Nirakara is the gateway shinma governing shape itself, distinct from and prerequisite-free relative to the five Grace shinma (Dharma/Nirvishesha/Nirvikalpa/Nishkriya/Nirguna); per the book's framing text (immediately preceding this section, p. 148/PDF 149), any Charm with a mutation-point cost belongs in a sense to Nirakara, but only the Charms in this section and the two sibling trees below (Elemental Influence, Emotional Influence) are formally 'Assumption-type Charms' with no minimum Grace requirement (their Combo experience cost is twice their minimum Essence requirement instead). Consolidated the five elemental variants into one row, matching this inventory's established precedent for multi-variant single-header Charms (e.g. bastion-of-the-self, great-works-of-the-grace).

name: Assumption of Cerements and Bone
summary: A second independent gateway Assumption-type Charm: lets the raksha pass through Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature within the Underworld, treated as dead for all effects while still materially present.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: This Charm allows a raksha to pass through the gateway Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature within the Underworld. Raksha with this Charm active are material in Creation but, otherwise, are treated as dead for all effects -- they can receive Essence from burnt offerings, Deathlords can feed on them for power, and so forth. This is an Assumption-type Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Assumption-Type Charms' section, p. 149 (PDF 150). Second independent root of the diagrammed 'Assumption Charms 1' tree, alongside Assumption of Elemental Shape.

name: Assumption of the Person's Heart
summary: Lets the raksha pass through Nirakara and exist as a minor Wyld taint on a single visible creature of Creation, optionally sharing the benefits of her mutations and active Charms with that creature (for gossamer) if it consents.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: Assumption of Elemental Shape (Any).
mechanics: This Charm allows a raksha to pass through the gateway Nirakara and exist as a minor Wyld taint on a creature of Creation. The creature must be visible when she uses this Charm. If this is her only active Assumption-type Charm, the raksha exists in Creation as an extension of that creature -- she cannot exist outside its presence, and she involuntarily becomes a dematerialized but manifest spirit when the creature becomes unconscious or someone attempts to forcibly separate her from it. If she has another Assumption-type Charm active, she can leave its presence and does not dematerialize (voluntarily or otherwise) in either circumstance. If the creature consents, this Charm allows the raksha to share the benefits of her mutations and active Charms with it, costing 1 gossamer for each mutation point or gossamer point of Charms shared (for example, spending 1 gossamer to extend Assumption of Elemental Shape (Water) to a shipwrecked sailor); she can withdraw these gifts at any time. This Charm is a work of glamour and cannot taint creatures whose Stamina + Essence exceeds the raksha's Charisma. This is an Assumption-type Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Assumption-Type Charms' section, p. 149 (PDF 150, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 151).

name: Assumption of the Land's Heart
summary: Lets the raksha pass through Nirakara and exist as a subliminal Wyld taint on a hamlet-sized region, sinking her Heart Grace into the land and 'programming' it to trigger works of glamour on specified conditions -- at the cost of losing her own volition and ability to spend Willpower while the Charm lasts.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: Assumption of Elemental Shape (Any).
mechanics: This Charm allows the raksha to pass through the gateway Nirakara and exist as a subliminal Wyld taint on a region of Creation sized to house and feed up to 25 people. The raksha sinks her Heart Grace into the region; mystically separated from her Heart Grace, she cannot spend Willpower and exists without volition, though she can respond to events, defend herself, answer questions and perform repetitive tasks without initiating new courses of action. This Charm lets the raksha 'program' her Heart Grace to trigger works of glamour (such as Fearsome Mien or Beguilement) based on conditions she specifies against any appropriate target within the region; she can access this information consciously with a successful difficulty 5 Intelligence + Lore roll. Discovering the nature of the taint requires a successful difficulty 3 Perception + Occult roll, and tracking it back to the raksha requires a successful difficulty 5 Perception + Occult roll (Charms such as All-Encompassing Sorcerer's Sight allow automatic success). This is an Assumption-type Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Assumption-Type Charms' section, p. 150 (PDF 151). Root of the Land's Heart line in the diagrammed 'Assumption Charms 1' tree, feeding Assumption of the City's Heart and Assumption of the Living Kingdom. Its own text cross-references Fearsome Mien and Beguilement (both already inventoried) by page number as examples of works of glamour this Charm can trigger.

name: Assumption of the City's Heart
summary: Functions as Assumption of the Land's Heart but blankets a city-sized region (up to 1,000 people); if invoked together with Assumption of the Land's Heart, the overlapping central region becomes a place of power where the raksha's Heart can invoke permanent glamours.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Assumption of the Land's Heart.
mechanics: This Charm functions as Assumption of the Land's Heart, but blankets a larger region -- a place sized to support up to 1,000 people. Fair Folk can invoke this Charm together with Assumption of the Land's Heart; the central region where both overlap becomes a place of power, where the raksha's Heart can invoke permanent glamours as well as works of glamour. This is an Assumption-type Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Assumption-Type Charms' section, p. 150 (PDF 151).

name: Assumption of the Living Kingdom
summary: Functions as Assumption of the Land's Heart but blankets a small-kingdom-sized region (up to 100,000 people); if invoked together with Assumption of the Land's Heart, the raksha regains the ability to commune with her Heart and take self-directed actions (though still not spend Willpower) while inside the overlapping central region.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Assumption of the Land's Heart.
mechanics: This Charm functions as Assumption of the Land's Heart, but blankets a much larger region -- a small kingdom, able to support 100,000 people. Fair Folk can invoke this Charm together with Assumption of the Land's Heart; the central region where both overlap becomes a place of power. So long as she remains within that central region, the raksha can commune with her Heart and make decisions; she cannot spend Willpower (although the Heart can), but she can take self-directed actions. This is an Assumption-type Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Assumption-Type Charms' section, p. 150 (PDF 151). Second branch off Assumption of the Land's Heart, parallel to Assumption of the City's Heart.

name: Assumption of the Wyld-Tainted Land
summary: As the Wyld recedes from a region, lets the raksha take a fading Bordermarches area with her through Nirakara, functioning as the larger Assumption-of-the-Land's-Heart-line Charms but additionally infusing the region with enough ambient Wyld energy for the raksha to shape it, at +5 difficulty.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Assumption of the City's Heart.
mechanics: As the Wyld recedes from a region, a raksha can take the land with her through the gateway Nirakara. This Charm functions as Assumption of the City's Heart (the book's text names 'Assumption of the Kingdom's Heart,' evidently referring to this same line), except the region chosen must be a section of Bordermarches fading into Creation. In addition to the other effects, this Charm creates a powerful tainted land, infused with sufficient ambient Wyld energy for the raksha to shape it, albeit at +5 difficulty. This is an Assumption-type Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Assumption-Type Charms' section, p. 150 (PDF 151). Its own text says this Charm 'functions as Assumption of the Kingdom's Heart,' but no Charm of that exact name appears anywhere in this book -- its stated Prerequisite Charms line (Assumption of the City's Heart) and the diagram both confirm it branches off Assumption of the City's Heart, so this is treated as a naming slip for that Charm rather than a reference to Assumption of the Living Kingdom; flagged here rather than silently corrected.

name: Mad God Mien
summary: A permanent Charm layered onto any active Assumption-type Charm that makes the raksha wholly alien to Creation: raises the cost of all her Assumption-type Charms, hardens her against Charms that twist her body, and makes Creation-born powers treat her as an automaton immune to most direct mental influence -- undoable only by specific fate-binding powers.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Any Assumption-type Charm.
mechanics: Some raksha learn to adopt shape while remaining wholly alien to Creation. As they pass through Nirakara and fill themselves with Creation's Essence, they twist it into the raw, mad structures of the Wyld. Learning this Charm permanently increases the cost of all Assumption-type Charms by 2 gossamer or 2 mutation points. This Charm adds 1 to the difficulty of Charms that twist or reshape the raksha's body. It also makes the Charms and powers of the Creation-born treat the raksha as an automaton and a creature outside of fate, immune to most direct mental influence effects; glamour sorcery cast with the permanent version of this Charm is immune to normal sorcerous countermagic. The effects of this Charm are a matter of structure rather than power -- it can be undone by powers that bind the raksha (or spell) into Creation, such as the Greater Sign of Jupiter (Exalted: The Sidereals) or Harmony with Reality Technique (Exalted: The Lunars).
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Assumption-Type Charms' section, p. 150 (PDF 151, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 152). Its Prerequisite Charms line reads 'Any Assumption-type Charm' rather than a specific named Charm -- this row's crossReferences point to assumption-of-elemental-shape as a representative example (the most common gateway Charm) rather than an exhaustive or exclusive list, since any of the Assumption-type Charms in this section (or the Emotional Influence sub-tree below) satisfies the prerequisite. extinction-of-desire (in the Ring Grace tree) already references this Charm by name ('gains the benefits of Mad God Mien') without a resolvable cross-reference at the time it was written; that reference now resolves to this row.

name: Sovereign Elemental Shape
summary: The root of the Elemental Influence Charms: lets the raksha reflexively grant a one-die Wyld bonus to a witnessed normal action when the target is defined as drawing on the element the raksha has assumed.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: Assumption of Elemental Shape (Any).
mechanics: The raksha can use the elements of Creation to assist others. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Elemental Assistance -- for 1 mote, the raksha can reflexively grant a one-die Wyld bonus to a single witnessed action. The player of the raksha or his target must define how the target uses one of the five elements to assist him, and the raksha must have the Assumption of Elemental Shape for that element active. For example, an archer might gain the assistance of a raksha who has assumed elemental Earth by taking a firm stance and 'rooting herself in the ground.'
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Elemental Influence' sub-tree, p. 151 (PDF 152). Root of the diagrammed 'Assumption Charms 2' tree, alongside World-Angering Elemental Mastery and Elemental Transformation, all three branching off Assumption of Elemental Shape.

name: Element-Weaving Style
summary: Lets the raksha shape an assumed element by touch into complex, intricate forms without tools, via three Craft-based normal-action abilities for air/fire/water, wood, and earth/metal.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: Sovereign Elemental Shape.
mechanics: The raksha can shape the element by touch, rapidly molding it into complex and intricate shapes without tools. These are normal actions rather than shaping actions: Compliant Element Shaping -- for 5 motes, a single Craft roll shapes air, fire or water; sculptures last a single lunar cycle; requires the matching Assumption of Elemental Shape (Air/Fire/Water) active. Compliant Woodland Shaping -- for 5 motes, a single Craft roll shapes wood as if with First Age tools (a -1 difficulty reduction replacing any tool penalty or benefit); requires Assumption of Elemental Shape (Wood) active. Compliant Mountain Shaping -- for 5 motes, a single Craft roll shapes earth and metal as if with First Age tools (same -1 difficulty reduction); requires Assumption of Elemental Shape (Earth) active.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Elemental Influence' sub-tree, p. 151 (PDF 152, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 153).

name: Elemental Invocation
summary: The capstone of the Sovereign Elemental Shape line: manifests a treasure of the Wyld in Creation, given shape and form appropriate to the raksha's assumed element, fading away at the end of the story.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Element-Weaving Style.
mechanics: The raksha manifests in Creation one of the treasures of the Wyld. This Charm lets the raksha invoke a possession in Creation, giving it shape and form appropriate to an element whose Essence the raksha has absorbed through Assumption of Elemental Shape. For example, a raksha of air might summon a lethal hazard as a storm, and a raksha of water might call forth a servant in the shape of a siaka. It fades away again at the end of the story. This Charm can call forth even possessions and servants that cannot normally exist in Creation.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Elemental Influence' sub-tree, p. 152 (PDF 153). 'Possession' here is a Fair Folk Background/wealth concept described elsewhere in the book (pp. 131-132) but not yet its own inventory row; flagged for a future pass alongside the Backgrounds already covered.

name: World-Angering Elemental Mastery
summary: The hostile counterpart to Sovereign Elemental Shape: lets the raksha reflexively impose an environmental penalty equal to her Essence on a witnessed normal action of which she disapproves, using her assumed element.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Assumption of Elemental Shape (Any).
mechanics: The raksha can use the elements of Creation to hinder others. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Elemental Hindrance -- for 5 motes, the raksha can reflexively impose an environmental penalty equal to his Essence on a single witnessed action of which he disapproves. The raksha's player must define how his character uses one of the five elements to impose this penalty, and he must have the Assumption of Elemental Shape appropriate to that element active.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Elemental Influence' sub-tree, p. 152 (PDF 153). Second branch off Assumption of Elemental Shape in the diagrammed 'Assumption Charms 2' tree, parallel to Sovereign Elemental Shape and Elemental Transformation.

name: Teeth of the World
summary: The capstone of the World-Angering Elemental Mastery line: grants five elemental attack abilities (one per Assumption of Elemental Shape variant) that use normal Dexterity-based dice pools rather than shaping actions, each requiring the matching elemental assumption active.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: World-Angering Elemental Mastery.
mechanics: The raksha attacks others with the elements of Creation. These abilities affect normal actions rather than shaping actions: Wind Knives (Air) -- for 5 motes, an undodgeable hail/lightning/wind attack with base lethal damage of twice the raksha's Essence and a normal Dexterity + Archery pool, requiring the target within 1,000 yards and visible. Inciting the Ocean's Hunger (Water) -- for 5 motes, an unblockable attack turning a nearby water source against an enemy within five yards of it, base lethal damage twice the raksha's Essence, Dexterity + Brawl pool, target within 100 yards. Thrashing Dragon Fire Dance (Fire) -- for 5 motes, a normal Dexterity + Archery attack against an enemy within five yards of a significant blaze, base damage twice the raksha's Essence (or, without a blaze, a weaker 2L conjured-flame version for 5 motes), range 100 yards. Leaping Forest (Wood) -- for 5 motes, a normal Dexterity + Brawl attack (trees initiate clinches, small wooden objects leap) against an enemy within five yards of a tree or 30 yards of a small wooden object, base lethal damage twice the raksha's Essence, range 100 yards. World-Shaking Heart (Earth) -- for 5 motes, a normal Dexterity + Brawl attack with base damage twice the raksha's Essence and range 500 yards (does not affect targets more than five yards from the ground); alternately, with one success on a normal Dexterity + Brawl action, the raksha can shake the ground within 30 yards, forcing standers to roll Dexterity + Athletics or fall and dealing the raksha's Essence in dice of lethal damage to structures.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Elemental Influence' sub-tree, p. 152 (PDF 153, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 154). Each of the five named abilities requires its own matching Assumption of Elemental Shape variant active, mirroring the pattern already established by Sovereign Elemental Shape and Element-Weaving Style.

name: Elemental Transformation
summary: A repeatable Charm letting the raksha adopt an alternate animal or elemental shape (designed with 3 mutation points, chosen at purchase), speaking to animals of that type and shapeshifting into it as a work of glamour with a two-die penalty on physical and social actions while transformed.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Assumption of Elemental Shape (Any).
mechanics: The raksha masters the art of transformation, learning to adopt an alternate shape suited to her elemental Essence. The raksha can purchase this Charm more than once, learning an additional shape each time; if an animal shape is chosen, the raksha can speak to animals of that type whenever this Charm is active. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Shapeshift -- for 10 motes and 1 Willpower, the raksha changes to the alternate form chosen at purchase (an animal or elemental body whose special abilities are designed with 3 mutation points -- for example, an eagle form built from Gossamer Wing Flight and keen vision via Surpassing Excellence, or a bear form with Armament of Flesh and the Large pox). This change is a work of glamour; it imposes a two-die penalty on the raksha's physical and social actions and grants the benefits of the mutations without spending actual mutation points. The raksha can still talk in the animal form.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Elemental Influence' sub-tree, p. 153 (PDF 154). Third branch off Assumption of Elemental Shape in the diagrammed 'Assumption Charms 2' tree; its own text example builds sample alternate forms directly out of Sword Grace tree Mutation Charms already inventoried (Gossamer Wing Flight, Surpassing Excellence, Armament of Flesh), demonstrating the cross-tree design intent between Nirakara's Assumption Charms and Nishkriya's Mutation Charms.

name: Mercurial Shape
summary: Makes the raksha's shape a thing of quicksilver and change, letting her reflexively grant herself a two-die Wyld bonus on a normal action by defining how a mutable form achieves it.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Sovereign Elemental Shape, Elemental Transformation.
mechanics: The raksha makes his shape a thing of quicksilver and change. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Mutable Form -- for 5 motes, the raksha can reflexively give himself a two-die Wyld bonus. The raksha must define how he uses a mutable form to achieve this bonus -- for example, arms that lengthen and retract for a Larceny roll to steal an Exalt's sword, an ever-changing shape for a Survival roll to avoid pursuit, or a light effort of shapeshifting for a Larceny roll to create a disguise.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Elemental Influence' sub-tree, p. 153 (PDF 154, with the mechanics description continuing onto PDF 155). Converges Sovereign Elemental Shape and Elemental Transformation in the diagrammed 'Assumption Charms 2' tree, confirmed against the rendered page image. Closes out the Elemental Influence sub-tree.

name: Assumption of Dreams and Passion
summary: A worked example of a personalized, non-elemental Assumption-type Charm tree: lets the raksha pass through Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature by filling his spirit with dream-derived emotional Essence, adding his highest feeding Grace in dice to Social rolls that provoke a chosen emotion.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: This Charm allows a raksha to pass through the gateway Nirakara and exist as a shaped creature within Creation. The raksha fills his spirit with the raw dream-derived Essence of an emotion or passion. This Charm adds the raksha's highest feeding Grace in dice to Social rolls where provoking that emotion is useful. The raksha chooses the emotion in question when invoking this Charm. This is an Assumption-type Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Emotional Influence' sub-tree, p. 154 (PDF 155). The book explicitly frames this whole sub-tree as 'an example of the type' of personalized non-elemental Assumption-type Charm tree a raksha can develop -- i.e. Emotional Influence is not the only possible non-elemental Assumption line, just the one worked example the text provides. Root of the diagrammed 'Assumption Charms 3' tree.

name: Elegant Muse Attitude
summary: Lets the raksha reflexively grant a one-die Wyld bonus to a witnessed normal action by defining how the target draws on raksha-inspired passion.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Assumption of Dreams and Passion.
mechanics: The raksha can use emotion to assist others. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Emotional Assistance -- for 1 mote, the raksha can reflexively grant a one-die Wyld bonus to a single witnessed action. The player of the raksha or his target must define how the target uses raksha-inspired passion to assist himself. The raksha must have Assumption of Dreams and Passion active.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Emotional Influence' sub-tree, p. 154 (PDF 155). Direct emotional-Essence analog of Sovereign Elemental Shape.

name: Emotion-Weaving Style
summary: Lets the raksha reshape a target's Nature for a story by carving their mind with embedded emotional Essence, an artificial change the target can consciously ignore but finds uncomfortable to resist.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 3; Prerequisite Charms: Elegant Muse Attitude.
mechanics: The raksha uses the emotional Essence embedded in his alien soul to shape, mold and carve the minds of others. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Great Craft of Minds -- the raksha spends 5 motes, and his player rolls Conviction + Performance as a normal action against a difficulty equal to the target's Essence. On a success, the raksha can change the target's Nature to a Nature of the raksha's choice; this change lasts for one story. The change is an artificial and artistic twisting of the target's spirit driven by emotional blocks set up within the target's mind -- targets can ignore its non-mechanical impact but find it uncomfortable to do so.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Emotional Influence' sub-tree, p. 154 (PDF 155). Direct emotional-Essence analog of Element-Weaving Style.

name: Emotional Invocation
summary: The capstone of the Elegant Muse Attitude line: manifests a treasure of the Wyld in Creation, its shape and Essence filled with the emotion the raksha has assumed, giving it an odd and appealing character to onlookers.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 3; Prerequisite Charms: Emotion-Weaving Style.
mechanics: The raksha manifests in Creation one of the treasures of the Wyld. This Charm lets the raksha invoke a possession into Creation, filling the gaps in its shape and Essence with the emotion the raksha has assumed via Assumption of Dreams and Passion. For example, a raksha enshrouded in lust could summon a cabinet or a mutated siaka, but both would have an odd and sensual appeal for those who looked upon them.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Emotional Influence' sub-tree, p. 155 (PDF 156). Direct emotional-Essence analog of Elemental Invocation.

name: Unwanted Obsession Provocation Technique
summary: The hostile counterpart to Elegant Muse Attitude: lets the raksha reflexively impose an environmental penalty equal to her Essence on a witnessed normal action of which she disapproves, using her assumed emotional mien.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 2; Prerequisite Charms: Assumption of Dreams and Passion.
mechanics: The raksha can use the emotional Essence flooding him to drive others to distraction. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Emotional Hindrance -- for 5 motes, the raksha can reflexively impose an environmental penalty equal to his Essence on a single witnessed action of which he disapproves. The raksha's player must define how his character uses the emotional mien imposed by Assumption of Dreams and Passion to inflict this penalty.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Emotional Influence' sub-tree, p. 155 (PDF 156). Second branch off Assumption of Dreams and Passion in the diagrammed 'Assumption Charms 3' tree, parallel to Elegant Muse Attitude; direct emotional-Essence analog of World-Angering Elemental Mastery.

name: Essence-Disrobing Passion
summary: The capstone of the Unwanted Obsession Provocation Technique line: an unparryable emotional attack that strips motes from a witnessed target and inflicts a stacking one-die penalty on their normal actions for the rest of the scene.
requirements: Minimum Essence: 3; Prerequisite Charms: Unwanted Obsession Provocation Technique.
mechanics: The raksha attacks the Essence patterns of others with madly surging dreams. This ability affects normal actions rather than shaping actions: Mote-Scattering Storm -- for 5 motes, the raksha can overwhelm the thoughts and Essence of a witnessed target with unruly emotion. This is a normal action with a Conviction + Performance dice pool and a base difficulty equal to the target's permanent Essence; this attack is intangible and cannot be parried without Charms or stunts capable of deflecting such attacks. If the raksha succeeds, the target loses motes equal to the raksha's Essence and suffers a one-die environmental penalty on normal actions for the rest of the scene. This penalty is cumulative with the penalty for Emotional Hindrance but not with itself.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirakara, the Mask' -> 'Emotional Influence' sub-tree, p. 155 (PDF 156). Closes out both the Emotional Influence sub-tree and the entire Assumption-type/Nirakara Charm section; 'NIRGUNA, THE HEART' (the already-inventoried Heart Grace tree's opening) begins immediately afterward on the same page.

name: Vexing (Effects of Damage, Vexing Places, the Unshaped, and Creatures of Creation)
summary: Losing a Sword-shaping contest lets the winner vex the loser: seizing a handful of her possessions, claiming a waypoint she holds, ripping a fresh three-dot behemoth out of an unshaped's torn Sword Grace, or -- against a Creation-born victim with no Sword Grace of her own -- forcing a resisted Willpower + Essence roll instead of a damage track.
mechanics: Effects of Damage: raksha mark Sword damage off against the sum of their Valor and Sword Traits; once a combatant has taken more Sword damage than that sum, she loses the shaping contest and the attacker vexes her. Vexing (general): the attacker seizes a number of the loser's possessions -- artifacts, possessions, waypoints or Graces she owns -- equal to the loser's Sword Grace, with total seized artifact levels capped at 5; the only sacrosanct possession is a character's own Heart Grace, which can be claimed only by whoever holds her Sword Grace, and even that protection lapses once the Sword Grace itself is broken. Vexing Places: vexing a waypoint claims possession of it; the raksha must commit 3 motes to each waypoint she claims, and for as long as that commitment lasts a portion of her spirit resides there, making her aware of all Sword shaping within it, letting her use her own applicable Sword defenses against shaping attacks made against that waypoint, and letting her make Sword-shaping actions as though physically present there. Vexing the Unshaped: vexing an unshaped rips open its Sword Grace; the power that pours out naturally shapes itself into a fresh three-dot behemoth, or the vexing raksha can instead channel it into an existing three- or four-dot behemoth to improve it by one dot. A given unshaped can be vexed at most once per story. Vexing Creatures of Creation: characters with no Sword Grace are still vulnerable to vexation, but since they have no Sword damage track, their players instead roll the character's Willpower + Essence against a difficulty equal to the raksha's damage successes each time she lands a Sword-shaping hit; Dragon-Blooded Exaltation grants a bonus die, Celestial Exaltation two bonus dice, and Solar or Abyssal Exaltation three. A successful roll takes no damage; a failed roll means the victim is vexed. Charms and effects that reduce a victim's soak against Sword-shaping attacks reduce this Willpower + Essence pool by the same amount instead, before Exalted add their bonus dice.
compatibility: All raksha engaged in Sword-shaping combat; Creation-born victims without a Sword Grace resist vexation with Willpower + Essence rather than marking a damage track, with Exaltation-based bonus dice for the Dragon-Blooded, Celestial and Solar/Abyssal Exalted.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Effects of Damage' (p. 147/PDF 148) -> 'Vexing Places' / 'Vexing the Unshaped' / 'Vexing Creatures of Creation' (p. 148/PDF 149) sections, immediately preceding the Questing sidebar (see questing-sidebar) and 'The Shinma' section that introduces Nirakara and the already-inventoried universal Assumption-type Charm tree. Per the same individual-shaping-weapon exclusion already flagged on shaping-combat-basics, this row does not separately inventory the Sword Grace's shaping-weapon stat table (Entanglement, Extras, Hazard, Horror, Monster, Mutant Warleader, Nishkriya Mask, Personal Prowess) that immediately precedes 'Effects of Damage' on p. 147/PDF 148.

name: Questing (sidebar)
summary: A boxed sidebar describing questing: raksha who deliberately seek out the unshaped in the Deep Wyld and engage them in ritual shaping contests, hoping to rip a powerful artifact, spell or servant free from a triumph, but risking terrible retaliation if they linger too long or lose.
mechanics: Raksha sometimes seek out the unshaped and engage them in ritual shaping contests; a triumphant raksha can rip a powerful artifact, spell or servant from the unshaped's soul (using the general Vexing rules -- see vexing-mechanic). In the Deep Wyld the unshaped are all but immortal, and only a few rare artifacts can subdue one permanently, so a questing raksha must plan her escape route carefully. The unshaped are believed to derive a certain power from the process of questing itself, which encourages them to tolerate it even when they lose; less tolerant god-monsters of the deep can instead chase an impudent quester all the way to the Middlemarches or even the Bordermarches, inflicting terrible ravishments and burdens on his soul.
compatibility: Any raksha willing to travel into the Deep Wyld to challenge an unshaped god-monster.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Questing' boxed sidebar, p. 148 (PDF 149), set beside the 'Vexing Places' / 'Vexing the Unshaped' / 'Vexing Creatures of Creation' sections on the same page.

name: Glamour Sorcery (overview)
summary: The raksha's great spells: artifacts forged from raksha Graces and bound to the aspects of Dharma (the Cup), purchased through the Artifact Background and used as poisons, drugs and tools of ravishment that undermine or change the Essence patterns of those they touch.
requirements: Purchased through the Artifact Background like any other artifact; the spell's Artifact level (one to five, or N/A for the rarest distillations) sets its dot cost.
mechanics: Glamour sorcery spells are artifacts, not Charms: a raksha (or Lunar Exalted) buys one with Artifact Background dots, then attunes to it with a commitment of 3 motes per Artifact level plus several scenes of ritual maintenance each day (many nobles delegate this upkeep to a common lorekeeper). The spell uses its lorekeeper's Traits when determining its abilities; the lorekeeper is not necessarily the raksha who holds spiritual ownership of the spell (having created, purchased, or won it) -- it is the owner who spends the motes and gossamer to summon the spell into Creation. Glamour Sorcery spells can be used as weapons in Cup-shaping combat. Each spell tier (Waking, Dreaming, Desire, Samadhi, Shinma Circle -- see waking-circle-spell, dreaming-circle-spell, desire-circle-spell, samadhi-circle-spell, shinma-circle-spell) has its own build-point budget, invocation cost, and Cup-shaping-weapon stat defaults; every tier requires at least one Assumption-type Charm mutation (typically Assumption of Elemental Shape) among its build points, tying the spell's tangible form back to the universal Assumption-type Charm tree.
cost: Artifact Background dots (per the spell's Artifact level) plus a per-tier commitment (3 motes per Artifact level) and per-tier invocation cost in motes/gossamer/scenes (see individual spell-tier rows).
compatibility: Any raksha (or Lunar Exalted) with Artifact Background dots to spend; the specific spell built with a tier's mutation points is chosen by its creator/owner within that tier's rules.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Glamour Sorcery' -> 'Spell Abilities' sections, p. 205 (PDF 206), immediately following the Sword Grace's Mutation Charms section (the last of Chapter Five's five per-Grace Charm trees). Folds in the short 'Spell Abilities' subsection (lorekeeper mechanic) rather than giving it its own row, since it is general framework text rather than a discrete rule or choice.

name: Glamour Sorcery and Countermagic (sidebar)
summary: A boxed sidebar mapping each glamour-sorcery spell tier to an equivalent tier of Creation sorcery for countermagic purposes, and explaining how targeting a spell's physical manifestation with countermagic of equal or greater level can suppress or permanently unmake it.
mechanics: For countermagic purposes, Waking and Dreaming Circle spells count as Terrestrial Circle Sorcery, Desire and Samadhi Circle spells count as Celestial Circle Sorcery, and Shinma Circle spells count as Solar Circle Sorcery. Every glamour-sorcery spell has a physical manifestation, usually as sturdy as an artifact made from one of the Five Magical Materials. Countermagic of equal level targeted at that manifestation makes it go inert, dispelling all its effects for the rest of that story (the raksha cannot use that spell again until a new story begins); countermagic of greater level shatters the manifestation outright, destroying the spell entirely and unmaking all its effects permanently. Specifically: Emerald Countermagic shatters Waking Circle spells; Sapphire Countermagic shatters Waking, Dreaming, and Desire Circle spells; and Adamant Countermagic, targeting the manifestation directly, utterly destroys any raksha spell not protected by Mad God Mien.
compatibility: Any Creation-born sorcerer with access to Terrestrial-, Celestial-, or Solar-Circle-tier countermagic; any raksha whose glamour sorcery spells lack Mad God Mien's protection.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Glamour Sorcery and Countermagic' boxed sidebar, p. 206 (PDF 207), set beside the Dreaming and Desire Circle spell entries.

name: Waking Circle Spell
summary: The pettiest tier of glamour sorcery -- more the caffeine or sugar of the Wyld than its cocaine -- built as a one-dot artifact whose tangible effects are crafted almost entirely from mutation points.
requirements: Artifact Background 1 (or as needed for the spell's Artifact rating of one dot).
mechanics: In Cup-shaping combat, a Waking Circle spell has qualities similar to a normal one-dot artifact weapon -- by default a piercing clinch enhancer with Speed -5, Accuracy +1, Damage +4, Defense +4, and Rate 1. Invoking the spell in Creation takes one scene, 10 motes, and 1 gossamer; once invoked it remains invoked for a full story, and the motes spent to invoke it are not committed. Build the spell's tangible effects as an object with 10 mutation points, exactly 1 of which must go to an Assumption-type Charm mutation (normally Assumption of Elemental Shape). The remaining 9 mutation points craft the spell's other effects. Example given: a leering wooden mask with the permanent versions of Assumption of Elemental Shape (Wood) and the Hateful Coin Curse; looking at the mask forces an Intelligence + Bureaucracy roll from its lorekeeper, stripping the viewer one dot of Resources per success unless the viewer's Wits + Essence exceeds the lorekeeper's Bureaucracy.
cost: Artifact Background dot(s) to own; 3 motes/level to attune; 10 motes + 1 gossamer + one scene to invoke.
compatibility: Any raksha or Lunar Exalted with Artifact Background dots to spend on a one-dot artifact.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Glamour Sorcery' -> 'Waking Circle Spell (Artifact •)', p. 205 (PDF 206).

name: Dreaming Circle Spell
summary: A two-dot glamour-sorcery tier crafted from the substance of dream, disruptive to elements of pattern; most offer a positive pharmaceutical effect to their user or a disruptive poison to their victims, alongside normal one-dot-artifact-weapon combat qualities.
requirements: Artifact Background dots for the spell's two-dot Artifact rating.
mechanics: In shaping combat, a Dreaming Circle spell has qualities similar to a normal one-dot artifact weapon. In addition, most offer either a pharmaceutical effect (usually +2 dice to a shaping Ability) or a poison effect (usually forcing a Stamina + Resistance check at difficulty 3 each time the shaping weapon damages a target, lest the target suffer an extra point of Cup damage). Invoking the spell in Creation takes one scene, 15 motes, and 1 gossamer; once invoked it remains invoked for a full story, and the motes are not committed. Build the spell's tangible effects with 11 mutation points, 1 or 2 of which must go to Assumption-type Charm mutations (normally Assumption of Elemental Shape or Assumption of the Land's Heart); the rest craft the spell's other effects. Example given: a spherical gem with the permanent versions of Assumption of the Land's Heart and Fall of Night Shadows the Truth, which blankets a hamlet-sized region so that its people naturally conceal and forget their own suffering, believing they live in a utopia; a lorekeeper's Conviction + Stealth successes raise the difficulty of any Investigation/Lore/Occult/Socialize roll to learn about that pain, though characters with Intelligence + Essence exceeding the lorekeeper's Stealth cannot be shielded this way.
