cost: Artifact Background dots to own; 3 motes/level to attune; 15 motes + 1 gossamer + one scene to invoke.
compatibility: Any raksha or Lunar Exalted with Artifact Background dots to spend on a two-dot artifact.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Dreaming Circle Spell (Artifact ••)', p. 206 (PDF 207), between the Glamour Sorcery and Countermagic sidebar and the Desire Circle Spell entry.

name: Desire Circle Spell
summary: A three-dot glamour-sorcery tier crafted to influence the deep, shifting undermind urges behind both dreams and nightmares; strong enough that even characters who would normally be immune to a work of glamour still suffer its effects unless they use a stunt or Charm to see through it.
requirements: Artifact Background dots for the spell's three-dot Artifact rating.
mechanics: In shaping combat, a Desire Circle spell has qualities similar to a normal two- or three-dot artifact weapon, defaulting to Speed +6, Accuracy +1, Damage +8, Defense +1, and Rate 5. Invoking the spell in Creation takes two scenes, 20 motes, and 2 gossamer; once invoked it remains invoked until some condition inherent to the spell is met (up to one year and one day if that condition is simply the passage of time), and the motes are not committed. Build the spell's tangible effects with 13 mutation points, 1 to 4 of which must go to Assumption-type Charm mutations (normally Assumption of Elemental Shape, Assumption of the Land's Heart, or Assumption of the City's Heart); the rest craft the spell's other effects. Unlike lesser tiers, Desire Circle effects overcome characters whose Traits would normally render them immune to a work of glamour -- they still suffer its effects unless they use a stunt or Charm (not necessarily a Wyld-specific defense) to see through it. Example given: a labyrinth drawn on gilt paper with the permanent versions of Assumption of the City's Heart and Undetectable Lie, which sinks its power into a city and convinces characters with Wits + Essence up to the lorekeeper's Manipulation that they are 'hopelessly lost' from the moment they enter, wandering in circles even with their destination in plain sight; characters above that threshold would normally be immune but, because this is a Desire Circle effect, must still use a stunt or Charm to escape it.
cost: Artifact Background dots to own; 3 motes/level to attune; 20 motes + 2 gossamer + two scenes to invoke.
compatibility: Any raksha or Lunar Exalted with Artifact Background dots to spend on a three-dot artifact.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Desire Circle Spell (Artifact •••)', p. 206 (PDF 207), continuing onto p. 207/PDF 208.

name: Samadhi Circle Spell
summary: A four-dot glamour-sorcery tier -- also called a 'True Self Spell' -- crafted to influence the endless primordial dreams of the Wyld, the Graces, and the mortal soul; only a raksha who owns his own Heart Grace can cast one.
requirements: Artifact Background dots for the spell's four-dot Artifact rating; the casting/owning raksha must own his own Heart Grace (i.e. it must not be held or claimed by another).
mechanics: In shaping combat, a Samadhi Circle spell has qualities appropriate to a three- or four-dot artifact weapon, defaulting to Speed +6, Accuracy +1, Damage +8, Defense +1, Rate 5, and a special power (such as the ability to ready the spell without a shaping action). Invoking the spell in Creation takes two scenes, 25 motes, and 2 gossamer; once invoked it remains invoked until some condition inherent to the spell is met (up to one year and one day if that condition is time-based), and the motes are not committed. Build the spell's tangible effects with 15 mutation points, 1 to 6 of which must go to Assumption-type Charm mutations; the rest craft the spell's other effects. As with the Desire Circle, seeing through a Samadhi Circle work of glamour requires an appropriate Charm or stunt. Example given: a spell that creates a tainted land and slowly gathers an army of Wyld addicts as the Wyld recedes from Creation -- its permanent Assumption of the Wyld-Tainted Land takes force and creates the tainted region, the permanent version of Shiftless Untamed Beauty makes the land itself addictive, the permanent version of Adored By All the Worlds draws a few more Wyld-loyalist followers to the region each scene, the permanent version of Ordinary Object Conjuration forges one suit of armor from the sky each scene, and Mad God Mien protects the whole result from standard countermagic.
cost: Artifact Background dots to own; 3 motes/level to attune; 25 motes + 2 gossamer + two scenes to invoke.
compatibility: Any raksha (or Lunar Exalted) who owns his own Heart Grace, with Artifact Background dots to spend on a four-dot artifact.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Samadhi Circle Spell (Artifact ••••)', p. 207 (PDF 208), immediately following the tail end of Desire Circle Spell and the 'Magistrate Eyes' cross-reference to core Exalted.

name: Shinma Circle Spell
summary: The most terrifying tier of glamour sorcery: a five-dot spell crafted to influence the substance before dreams, the primal substrata of the Wyld, and the stuff from which the shinma, the Primordials, and certain of the unshaped were made.
requirements: Artifact Background dots for the spell's five-dot Artifact rating (or N/A for story-purpose, legendary-tier examples).
mechanics: In shaping combat, a Shinma Circle spell has qualities appropriate to a four- or five-dot artifact weapon, defaulting to Speed +6, Accuracy +1, Damage +8, Defense +1, Rate 5, and a major special power (such as a mote-fueled persistent defense or the ability to fight on its own). Invoking the spell in Creation takes three scenes, 30 motes, and 3 gossamer; once invoked it remains invoked until some condition inherent to the spell is met (up to one century if that condition is time-based), and the motes are not committed. Build the spell's tangible effects with up to 18 mutation points, at least 1 of which must go to an Assumption-type Charm mutation; the rest craft the spell's other effects. An appropriate Charm or stunt is needed to see through a Shinma Circle work of glamour, as with the Samadhi and Desire Circles. These player-facing build rules apply only to player-created Shinma Circle spells or to spells the Storyteller creates for casual unshaped use; Shinma Circle spells that exist purely for story purposes can have additional or unusual abilities and are sometimes effectively legendary (N/A) artifacts in power.
cost: Artifact Background dots to own; 3 motes/level to attune; 30 motes + 3 gossamer + three scenes to invoke.
compatibility: Any raksha or Lunar Exalted with Artifact Background dots to spend on a five-dot artifact; story-purpose Shinma Circle spells above this budget are Storyteller-only.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Shinma Circle Spell (Artifact •••••)', p. 207 (PDF 208), immediately preceding the 'Wyld Artifacts' section.

name: Wyld Artifacts (overview)
summary: Traditional-style artifacts -- swords, enchanted masks, and similar treasures -- that the Ring forges from raksha Graces and the substance of the Wyld; they rarely display the full predictability of Creation-forged artifacts, and only a few of them double as Ring-shaping weapons.
requirements: Purchased through the Artifact Background like glamour sorcery, adjurations, and behemoths.
mechanics: A raksha receives a +2 Rate, +1 Accuracy, and +1 Defense bonus to the qualities of a Ring-shaping weapon that she personally crafted or reshaped, on top of its base qualities. Wyld artifacts more generally include things like artifact swords and enchanted masks forged from Ring Graces and the substance of the Wyld; because the Ring's urge to shape is more generic than the Cup's, Staff's, or Sword's, only a few Wyld artifacts function as Ring-shaping weapons themselves. Those that do are usually built on the same principles as the curdling dream bow, the shaping lens, and the world heart (see resonant-chorus-bow, hundred-color-shaping-lens, and artifact-waypoint for named examples of each).
cost: Artifact Background dots (per the artifact's level).
compatibility: Any raksha with Ring Grace and Artifact Background dots to spend; the self-crafting bonus applies only to weapons the raksha personally crafted or reshaped.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Wyld Artifacts' section header and opening paragraphs, p. 207 (PDF 208), immediately following the Shinma Circle Spell entry.

name: Resonant Chorus Bow
summary: A gossamer-inlaid variant of the curdling dream bow, chiming and thrumming with the deep power and order bound inside it.
requirements: Artifact Background 1.
mechanics: Accuracy +2, Damage 15, Rate 2, unlimited Maximum Perception, a range of 6 waypoints, and a commitment cost of 3 motes.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a one-dot Wyld artifact.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Resonant Chorus Bow (Artifact •)', p. 207 (PDF 208).

name: Hundred Color Shaping Lens
summary: A writhing microcosm of an artifact, its ornate inlay made from a hundred woven strands of dream struggling eternally to dominate the pattern.
requirements: Artifact Background 2.
mechanics: Accuracy +2, Damage +3, Rate 2, unlimited Maximum Perception, a range of 10 waypoints, and a commitment cost of 6 motes.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a two-dot Wyld artifact.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Hundred Color Shaping Lens (Artifact ••)', p. 207 (PDF 208).

name: Artifact Waypoint
summary: An enchanted waypoint or collection of waypoints that forms a mobile Ring-shaping weapon, functioning like an airship-scale artillery platform that floats through the Wyld at a fixed distance from the waypoints it passes.
requirements: Artifact Background 3+ (Artifact level three or higher).
mechanics: An artifact waypoint floats through the Wyld at a fixed distance of one journey 'away,' 'above,' or 'below' the waypoints it passes through; the attuned raksha steers it at his normal movement rate. Used in Ring-shaping combat, it has qualities similar to a normal artifact ranged or thrown weapon of equal level, and a commitment cost of 3 motes per level. An artifact waypoint structure contains up to its Artifact level in individual waypoints, and attempts to damage the waypoints themselves through shaping are made at +3 difficulty.
cost: Artifact Background 3+; 3 motes per level to commit.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a level-three-or-higher Wyld artifact.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Artifact Waypoint (Artifact •••+)', p. 208 (PDF 209), continuing onto p. 209/PDF 210. This is the last named Wyld Artifact example before the 'Adjurations' section begins.

name: Adjurations (overview)
summary: The 'world-shaping oaths' that bind raksha society together: artifacts of the Fair Folk shaped from Graces and bound to the aspects of Nirvikalpa (the Staff), which empower whoever swears to them and then manipulate the oathtaker and the world itself to ensure their own fulfillment.
requirements: Purchased through the Artifact Background like glamour sorcery, Wyld artifacts, and behemoths.
mechanics: Adjurations have an Artifact level ranging from one to five, with certain lost oaths qualifying as Artifact N/A. Swearing to an adjuration requires a commitment of 1 mote per level, and the character cannot voluntarily stop committing Essence to it -- she must fulfill the oath before she can reclaim the investment. A raksha sworn to an adjuration cannot voluntarily break that oath; breaking it involuntarily causes the character to suffer a catastrophic botch at the most poetically appropriate moment, exactly as though an Eclipse Caste Solar had sanctified the oath. The environmental penalty for working around the adjuration is usually equal to its Artifact level. When a raksha attuned to a Throne Room swears to an adjuration on behalf of a Freehold, the Freehold holds the benefit in common, and the lord of the Freehold can reflexively assign it to any consenting character in fealty to him. Adjurations are weapons in Staff-shaping combat. Each of the five oath tiers (Samhara/Sword, Sthiti/Ring, Anugraha/Cup, Tirobhava/Staff, Srishti/Heart -- see samhara-oath, sthiti-oath, anugraha-oath, tirobhava-oath, srishti-oath) grants its own mutation-point budget, shaping-weapon stat defaults, and thematic promise structure, corresponding to Artifact levels one through five respectively.
cost: Artifact Background dots (per the adjuration's level) to own; 1 mote per level to commit and sustain the sworn oath.
compatibility: Any raksha (or Lunar Exalted) with Artifact Background dots to spend, willing to accept an unbreakable oath in exchange for its granted mutations.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Adjurations' section header and opening paragraphs, p. 208 (PDF 209), immediately following Artifact Waypoint.

name: How Inconvenient Are a Raksha's Oaths? (sidebar)
summary: A tone-setting sidebar clarifying that raksha oaths are not actually inconvenient in practice: raksha squirm out of complicated promises with finesse and exploit an enemy's trivial ones, and the dramatic 'legendary oath' stories associated with adjurations are driven by passion (or an Exalt's trickery), not by any need to access an adjuration's power.
mechanics: This sidebar contains no new mechanic; it is Storyteller/player guidance clarifying design intent. In Creation and in the raw Wyld, raksha try hard to avoid promises that would hamstring them, adjuration or otherwise. The complicated, powerful oaths and clever escapes seen in raksha stories are simply one more token in Staff-shaping contests, not evidence that raksha oaths function differently from the mechanics described in adjurations-overview.
compatibility: Any raksha; framing guidance for how to roleplay adjurations and oaths in play.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'How Inconvenient Are a Raksha's Oaths?' boxed sidebar, p. 208 (PDF 209), set beside the Samhara Oath entry.

name: Samhara Oath (Sword oath)
summary: A one-dot adjuration sworn in the name of Nishkriya, the Sword -- oaths made in the shadow of endings and the knowledge that all things die, often manifesting as raven shadows that hover near the raksha and drive others into commitments through fear.
requirements: Artifact Background 1.
mechanics: In shaping combat, a samhara oath has qualities similar to a normal one-dot artifact weapon -- typically Speed +7, Accuracy +2, Damage +9, Defense +3, Rate 2, and piercing damage. Each samhara oath contains a specific promise and up to 2 mutation points of powers; a raksha who attunes to the oath by swearing to that promise receives the associated mutations until the oath is broken or fulfilled. An unwise oath can put a raksha in Bedlam or calcify him. Example given: the raksha Dasasya swore, 'I shall not set foot again on land until I have slain the Unconquered Sun,' gaining the 2-point mutation Gossamer Wing Flight. Also called a Sword oath or one-dot oath.
cost: Artifact Background 1; 1 mote to commit and sustain.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a one-dot adjuration.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Samhara Oath (Artifact •)', p. 208 (PDF 209), continuing onto p. 209/PDF 210.

name: Sthiti Oath (Ring oath)
summary: A two-dot adjuration sworn in honor of the shinma of the Ring -- oaths recognizing that the self exists only in context with the other, often manifesting as coronas of light around those who sanctify their integrity with commitments.
requirements: Artifact Background 2.
mechanics: In shaping combat, a sthiti oath has qualities similar to a normal two-dot artifact weapon -- typically Speed +6, Accuracy +0, Damage +13, Defense -1, Rate 1, and piercing damage. Each sthiti oath contains a specific promise and up to 3 mutation points of powers; a raksha who attunes to the oath by swearing to that promise receives the associated mutations until the oath is broken or fulfilled. Example given: the raksha Ayo swore, 'Until Calibration takes this burden from me, I shall not sleep without weapon in hand,' gaining the mutation version of Ordinary Object Conjuration (needing only to beckon and roll Conviction + Performance at three successes to summon an excellent straight sword to her hand). Also called a Ring oath or two-dot oath.
cost: Artifact Background 2; 2 motes to commit and sustain.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a two-dot adjuration.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Sthiti Oath (Artifact ••)', spanning the bottom of p. 208 (PDF 209) and top of p. 209 (PDF 210).

name: Anugraha Oath (Cup oath)
summary: A three-dot adjuration sworn in the name of Dharma, the Cup -- oaths made in joy or hunger, out of desire for their outcome, often manifesting as will-o'-wisps or siren scraps of music that lure others into commitments through beauty.
requirements: Artifact Background 3.
mechanics: In shaping combat, an anugraha oath has qualities similar to a normal three-dot artifact weapon -- typically a piercing weapon with Speed +10, Accuracy +0, Damage +9, Defense +1, and Rate 3. Each anugraha oath contains a specific promise and up to 4 mutation points of powers; a raksha who attunes to the oath by swearing to that promise receives the associated mutations until the oath is broken or fulfilled, but halves the total mutation point cost (rounding up). Example given: the raksha Nishumba swore to dedicate himself for a year and a day to the devastation of his enemies, taking on a monstrous two-headed goblin body via the Huge Wyld affliction and 2 mutation points of Oath Gossamer. Also called a Cup oath or three-dot oath.
cost: Artifact Background 3; 3 motes to commit and sustain.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a three-dot adjuration.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Anugraha Oath (Artifact •••)', p. 209 (PDF 210).

name: Tirobhava Oath (Staff oath)
summary: A four-dot adjuration sworn in the name of Nirvikalpa, the Staff -- oaths sworn because oaths are bindings, and in bindings there is power, often manifesting as a staff wrapped with the terrible power of law.
requirements: Artifact Background 4.
mechanics: In shaping combat, a tirobhava oath has qualities similar to a normal four-dot artifact weapon -- typically Speed +10, Accuracy +0, Damage +9, Defense +1, Rate 3, piercing damage, and a minor special power. Each tirobhava oath contains a specific promise and up to 6 mutation points of powers; a raksha who attunes to the oath by swearing to that promise receives the associated mutations until the oath is broken or fulfilled, but halves the total mutation point cost (rounding up). Example given: the raksha Madhu, who dwelt in the endless ocean, swore, 'Let any catch me on the land, and they may slay me,' gaining Assumption of the Living Kingdom paired with an Assumption of the Land's Heart he personally knew; a Solar prince eventually covered the sea in obsidian shards and dredged him up to force his submission to destruction. Also called a Staff oath or four-dot oath.
cost: Artifact Background 4; 4 motes to commit and sustain.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a four-dot adjuration.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Tirobhava Oath (Artifact ••••)', p. 209 (PDF 210), continuing onto p. 210/PDF 211.

name: Srishti Oath (Heart oath)
summary: A five-dot adjuration sworn in the name of Nirguna, the Heart -- the truest and deepest oaths of the raksha, sworn for as little as a single mutation point.
requirements: Artifact Background 5.
mechanics: In shaping combat, a srishti oath has qualities similar to a normal four-dot artifact weapon -- typically Speed +10, Accuracy +0, Damage +9, Defense +1, Rate 3, piercing damage, and a major special power. Its benefits are built on up to 4 points of mutations, but the raksha may swear to the oath for a single mutation point. Example given: Hiranya swore to serve the shinma Nirvikalpa with endless austerities, and the oath's strength was such that neither man nor beast could kill him -- not with a weapon or without one, not by day nor night, not indoors nor outdoors, and not on the earth nor in the sky -- granting the benefit Bastion of the Self with partial immunity to mortal damage and the arts of the Sword; the monstrous raksha Nara-simha nonetheless caught him at the threshold in the twilight hour and strangled him on his lap, a three-die Wyld stunt that broke the oath and caused Hiranya to botch his own reflexive counterattack, snapping his own Sword Grace. Also called a Heart oath or five-dot oath.
cost: Artifact Background 5; 1-4 motes to commit and sustain, depending on how many mutation points the oath grants.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a five-dot adjuration.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Srishti Oath (Artifact •••••)', p. 210 (PDF 211), the last of the five oath tiers and immediately preceding the 'Behemoths' section.

name: Behemoths (overview and Behemoth Powers)
summary: Monstrous artifacts forged from raksha Graces and bound to the aspects of Nishkriya (the Sword), purchased through the Artifact Background and dominated/attuned much like any other artifact; they exist to make a point, manifesting the attitude of the raksha (or unshaped) who creates them, and use the base Traits of their attuned creature handler.
requirements: Purchased through the Artifact Background like glamour sorcery, Wyld artifacts, and adjurations.
mechanics: Behemoths have an Artifact level ranging from one to five, with the greatest monsters of the far reaches qualifying as Artifact N/A. Dominating a behemoth requires a commitment of 3 motes per level plus several hours of bonding time per day; nobles typically have creature handlers attune behemoths on their behalf. Behemoths are weapons in Sword-shaping combat. Behemoth Powers: a behemoth uses the base Traits of its attuned creature handler, specifically excluding Backgrounds and most Merits and Flaws, but including Virtues -- a Compassionate raksha's behemoths tend to be sympathetic monsters, while a Valorous raksha's are terrible, fearless foes. Each behemoth tier (Fey Beast, Daikaiju, Deep Wyld Horror -- see fey-beast, daikaiju, deep-wyld-horror) grants its own mutation-point budget and shaping/Sword-combat stat defaults, corresponding to increasing Artifact levels; ishiika documents a unique, story-specific Artifact N/A behemoth as a worked example of the top of the scale rather than a build a player follows.
cost: Artifact Background dots (per the behemoth's level) to own; 3 motes per level plus daily bonding time to dominate/attune.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend, or a creature handler attuned on a noble's behalf.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Behemoths' section header, opening paragraphs, and 'Behemoth Powers' subsection, p. 210 (PDF 211), immediately following Srishti Oath. Genuinely player-facing: the Artifact Background row (artifact-background-fair-folk) already names 'behemoths' among the treasures raksha buy with Artifact dots, and this section supplies the mechanical framework it references, resolving a forward reference left open by great-works-of-the-grace and unshaped-grace-transformation (both of which name-check p. 210's behemoth material by page number without a cross-reference, since no rows existed yet).

name: Fey Beast
summary: The least of the Wyld horrors a raksha marshals in battle -- a one- or two-dot behemoth built around a guaranteed natural weapon (Knife-Hand Dream plus Armament of Flesh) with a handful of mutation points left over to fit its theme.
requirements: Artifact Background 1 (one-dot fey beast) or 2 (two-dot fey beast).
mechanics: In shaping combat, a fey beast has qualities similar to a normal one-dot artifact weapon -- by default Speed -5, Accuracy +1, Damage +4, Defense +4, and Rate 2. Build a one-dot fey beast on up to 9 mutation points, or a two-dot fey beast on 11; 1 of those mutation points must go to Knife-Hand Dream and 2 to Armament of Flesh, giving the creature a natural attack with Speed -3, Accuracy +1, Damage +4L, Defense +1, and Rate 4 (it can also parry lethal attacks while unarmed). The remaining 6 (or 8) mutation points fit the creature's theme. Example given: a long-necked, sharp-beaked, scaled riding bird with Knife-Hand Dream, Armament of Flesh, Gossamer Wing Flight, Glorious Hero Form, and the Wyld affliction Thick Skin, using its handler's Traits but adding flight, 3L/3B soak, three dice on Survival rolls, a dot each of Strength and Stamina, and a beak-based natural attack.
cost: Artifact Background 1-2; 3-6 motes per level to dominate/attune.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a one- or two-dot behemoth.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Fey Beasts (Artifact • or ••)', p. 211 (PDF 212), the first named behemoth tier.

name: Daikaiju
summary: A three-dot behemoth at the heart of a raksha's army -- a monster of terrible prowess with heavy natural armor, weaponized natural attacks, and a generous mutation-point budget.
requirements: Artifact Background 3.
mechanics: In shaping combat, a daikaiju has qualities similar to a normal two- or three-dot artifact weapon -- by default Speed +10, Accuracy +3, Damage +12, Defense +0, and Rate 4. Daikaiju have 12L/12B armor, which stacks with armor from mutations. Their natural weaponry uses the attack modifiers of an exceptional mundane weapon (for example, great elephantine legs used as exceptional sledges with bonus accuracy, damage, and defense). Daikaiju receive 12 mutation points to spend as desired. Example given: a white hybroc dwelling in an eternal blizzard, with feathers like exceptional throwing knives (improved Rate, melee damage, and ranged damage, cast off at the nadir of a wingbeat), Imposition of Law for automatic success on Presence (Intimidation) rolls, Bastion of the Self for immunity to normal damage, Gossamer Wing Flight, and the Wyld affliction Huge (increasing Strength and Stamina by two dots over its handler's and adding two extra low health levels).
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a three-dot behemoth.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Daikaiju (Artifact •••)', p. 211 (PDF 212), continuing onto p. 212/PDF 213, illustrated with a full daikaiju artwork on p. 211/PDF 212.

name: Deep Wyld Horror
summary: A four- or five-dot behemoth serving as a raksha's terror weapon -- the heaviest-armored and most mutation-rich of the named behemoth tiers, with natural weaponry equivalent to an attuned Magical Material artifact.
requirements: Artifact Background 4 or 5.
mechanics: In Sword combat, a Deep Wyld horror has qualities appropriate to a four- or five-dot artifact; in shaping combat, it defaults to Speed +10, Accuracy +3, Damage +12, Defense +0, Rate 4, and possesses a special power of some sort. Deep Wyld horrors have 20L/20B armor, which stacks with armor from mutations. Their natural weaponry uses the modifiers for an attuned one- or two-dot artifact weapon, complete with Magical Material bonus. Deep Wyld horrors receive 15 mutation points to spend as desired. Example given: a soul-eating monstrous boar whose writhing barbed spines have the weapon qualities of an attuned soulsteel dire lance (Speed +12, Accuracy +3, Damage +9L, Defense +3, Rate 3, extra damage on a charge, and the ability to drink its handler's Essence in motes from any creature it damages), built as an indefatigable hunter with two picks of Imposition of Law, the Giant blight, the Enhanced Smell and Hearing pox, and Glorious Hero Form.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a four- or five-dot behemoth.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Deep Wyld Horror (Artifact •••• or •••••)', p. 212 (PDF 213). Note: this printed-page/PDF-page pair reflects the folio number printed on the physical page image, which reads 211 for the page bearing the 'Deep Wyld Horror,' 'Ishiika,' and 'Nirupadhika, the Way' material (PDF page 212); the source-manifest's earlier estimate of pp. 210-212/PDF 211-213 for Behemoths and p. 212/PDF 213 for Nirupadhika was off by one page and is corrected here after direct visual confirmation against the rendered page images.

name: Ishiika (unique legendary behemoth)
summary: A unique, story-specific Artifact N/A behemoth -- a scorpion formed of a surging sea of teeth, aspected to the shinma Nishkriya, once tamed by the lost Prince Balor but too vast even for him to wield against Creation. Documented here as a worked example of the top of the behemoth power scale, not as a build a player follows.
mechanics: Employed in Sword combat, Ishiika has Speed +10, Accuracy +3, Damage +12, Defense +5, and an unlimited Rate; its wielder automatically wins initiative (rolling normally only against a similar initiative-stealing effect), and the wielder can delay his initiative without penalty, acting at any point in the initiative order. Shaping weapons used to parry Ishiika are utterly destroyed, shattering their Sword and Heart Graces (if any) before eliminating them entirely. In ordinary combat, Ishiika has immortality on the level of the Primordials; it focuses three attacks on each mortal enemy per turn, each with 10 successes on the attack roll and 11L base damage, and targets who do not use Charms or stunts to defend themselves take an automatic three health levels of damage rather than suffer an attack.
compatibility: Storyteller-controlled, story-specific legendary artifact; not purchasable through the Artifact Background and not intended as a player build template, unlike fey-beast, daikaiju, and deep-wyld-horror.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Ishiika (Artifact N/A)', p. 212 (PDF 213). Classified gm-only rather than selectable: unlike the three generic behemoth tiers above it, Ishiika is presented as a unique creature tied to a specific lost NPC (Prince Balor) and explicitly too vast even for its own tamer to wield against Creation -- an illustrative extreme, not a purchasable template, matching the task's instruction to skip pure creature stat blocks meant for Storyteller use only.

name: Nirupadhika, the Way (sixth shinma)
summary: A brief, explicitly-illustrative sixth shinma beyond the book's five-Grace baseline (Cup/Ring/Staff/Sword/Heart): Nirupadhika defines space and location, is associated with the Abilities Awareness, Sail, and Survival, and the book presents it only as 'an example of one of the other shinma the raksha might tame' rather than as a standard character-creation option.
mechanics: Nirupadhika exists in no place and all places, its mad eyes regarding all things in the Wyld with disorienting simultaneity; it would speak but has no voice, would act but has no space in which to act -- compressed to nothingness and stretched in all directions, its perpetual agony is travel. The book explicitly frames it as one example of the 'other shinma' a raksha might theoretically tame beyond the five (Cup, Ring, Staff, Sword, Heart) used throughout character creation and the rest of this inventory, and notes that Charms for such a Grace are 'extremely rare' -- only two are given (forging-the-way-grace, perfect-reckoning-technique), both far shorter and less developed than any single section of the five main Grace Charm trees.
compatibility: Not part of the standard character-creation baseline; a rare, optional extra a Storyteller could sanction, most plausibly reached by a Creation-born character being granted a Way Grace via Forging the Way Grace rather than a raksha choosing it as one of her own starting Graces at chargen.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirupadhika, the Way' section, p. 211 (PDF 212), immediately following Ishiika and immediately before Chapter Six begins. DETERMINATION on the sixth 'Way' Grace: this is neither a standard sixth playable Grace nor pure GM/setting lore -- it sits in between. It is real, rules-complete, player-facing content (two fully statted Charms usable in actual play, one of which any raksha with the prerequisite Forging the Heart Grace Charm could learn and use to grant a Way Grace to a consenting creature), but the book itself explicitly disclaims it as an 'example' of the shinma system's extensibility rather than a core option, it is never mentioned in the character-creation chapters (Three/Four) already inventoried, no raksha is shown starting play with a Way Grace, and only two Charms exist for it (versus 12-78 for each of the five real Graces). It is inventoried as real, narrowly-scoped player-facing content (its two Charms as selectable rows) rather than folded into the five-Grace model used elsewhere in this inventory or excluded as GM-only, since a Creation-born character actually being granted a Way Grace via Forging the Way Grace is a genuine, usable-in-play outcome, not merely Storyteller-side lore.

name: Forging the Way Grace
summary: Crafts a Way Grace -- the sixth, exotic shinma Nirupadhika -- as an artifact for a consenting creature, teaching it to tame Nirupadhika and use its shaping actions to speed travel through the Wyld; requires the raksha to already know Forging the Heart Grace.
requirements: Minimum Ring: 0; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: Forging the Heart Grace.
mechanics: Crafting the Way Grace for a consenting creature, the raksha teaches the target to tame Nirupadhika. This Charm consumes a supply of gossamer and creates an artifact; the artifact has the normal qualities of a finely crafted weapon, suit of armor, or tool, in addition to the standard Grace qualities, and it creates a Way Trait for the creature. Raksha and other Essence users can attune to a creature's Way Grace: this requires six scenes of handling and a 1-mote commitment, which erases any previous raksha's attunement. Characters attuned to a creature's Way Grace can reflexively strip away the creature's connection to Nirupadhika, lowering its Way to 0; the Curse associated with this reduction is left to the Storyteller to determine. Raksha with a Way Grace can use their shaping actions to speed their travel through the Wyld -- a single success on a Dexterity + Sail Way-shaping action moves them one journey through the Wyld.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Simple. Any raksha who already knows Forging the Heart Grace; the resulting Way Grace and its associated Charm (Perfect Reckoning Technique) are usable by whichever consenting creature receives it.
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirupadhika, the Way' -> 'Forging the Way Grace', p. 211 (PDF 212). Parallels the already-inventoried Forging the (Grace) Grace Charms (forging-the-cup-grace, forging-the-ring-grace, forging-the-staff-grace, forging-the-sword-grace), all of which similarly grant a Creation-born character a Grace as an artifact; this is the first hint that the 'Forging the (Grace) Grace' pattern could in principle extend beyond the five core Graces to any shinma a raksha tames, including exotic ones like Nirupadhika.

name: Perfect Reckoning Technique
summary: The raksha sees for a moment through Nirupadhika's eyes, letting her plot a course to any landmark in the Wyld or Creation that she already knows.
requirements: Minimum Way: 3; Minimum Essence: 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The raksha sees for a moment through Nirupadhika's eyes. This Charm lets her plot a course to any landmark in the Wyld or Creation that she knows.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Simple. Only usable by a character with a Way Grace of 3 or higher (see nirupadhika-the-way, forging-the-way-grace).
notes: Chapter Five: Raksha Magic, 'Nirupadhika, the Way' -> 'Perfect Reckoning Technique', p. 211 (PDF 212), the last Charm in Chapter Five before Chapter Six: The Mountain Folk begins. Printed p. 212/PDF 213, the page immediately after this one, is a full-page illustration with no chapter text (confirmed by direct render), marking the true end of Chapter Five.

name: Gossamer Manta
summary: A large, stained-glass-manta-ray-shaped raksha vehicle that floats a yard above the ground and can skim over any relatively flat surface -- including prairie, tundra, water, liquid gemstone or molten lava -- and travels fastest of all across Rakshastan's silver fire.
requirements: Artifact Background 3; to pilot, Sail 2 and at least a one-dot specialty in Gossamer Manta.
mechanics: An oval-bodied craft 25 feet long and 15 feet wide, seating up to seven raksha (one pilot forward, three rows of passenger seats behind); its wings flap slowly as it moves. Waves of Essence push against the surface beneath it, propelling it forward at up to 40 mph over ordinary ground or liquid, or up to two waypoints per scene (80 mph) when traveling over silver fire, whose properties enhance those Essence waves. It is immune to the heat of lava and to destruction by all types of Rakshastan's liquid fire, and its raised sides count as 50% cover for occupants in combat. The pilot must commit 7 motes of Essence to fly it. As a Ring-shaping weapon it has Accuracy -2, Damage -2, Defense +4, Rate 1, Cost Artifact 3, Range 0 (a hand-to-hand Ring weapon affecting only targets in the same waypoint), Max Perception 3, and the Piercing quality (halving the target's Willpower for computing soak).
cost: Artifact Background 3; 7 motes of Essence to commit/pilot.
compatibility: Any raksha with Artifact Background dots to spend on a three-dot Wyld artifact vehicle; requires Sail 2 and a Gossamer Manta specialty to actually pilot it.
notes: Chapter One: Rakshastan, a boxed sidebar sitting between the 'The Deep Wyld' and 'Hazards of the South' section headers, p. 38 (PDF 39). This is the only genuinely player-facing, purchasable Artifact-Background item stat block found anywhere in Chapters One, Two, Six, or Seven during this triage pass; it is functionally the same Ring-forged-treasure category as Chapter Five's Wyld Artifacts (see wyld-artifacts-overview, resonant-chorus-bow, hundred-color-shaping-lens, artifact-waypoint), just presented alongside Chapter One's regional geography instead. Everything else nearby in Chapter One's Southern Marches material (Flame Gryphon, Lion Warrior, Sand Shark, Abacasteri, the Glittering Desert, Rookery, etc.) are Storyteller-facing 'Hazard Rating' creature/environment stat blocks, not player character options, and were deliberately excluded from this inventory as gm-only setting/encounter content.

name: Fair Folk Experience and Training Time
summary: Raksha use their own post-creation experience-cost table for Abilities, Graces, Charms and Specialties (distinct from core Exalted's, and different again for common versus noble raksha), and unlike ordinary Exalted, they have no 'training time' delay at all: any raksha may raise a Trait or learn something new at the start of each story, purely gated on having the experience to pay for it.
mechanics: Fair Folk Experience table: Caste or Common Ability increase costs (current rating x 2); other Ability increase costs (current rating x 3); Major Grace increase costs (current rating x 3); Minor Grace increase costs (current rating x 6); raising the Heart Grace to 4 costs a flat 20 points, and only once the raksha is eligible (has spent over 200 experience points total). New Trait costs: a new Charm costs 6; a new Specialty costs 2 for a common raksha or 5 for a noble raksha. All other costs (Attributes, Virtues, Willpower, Essence, Backgrounds, etc.) follow the ordinary Exalted core-rules experience table (p. 270). Fair Folk Training Time: raksha do not need to actively practice or study to advance -- there is no 'training time' requirement of any kind. Instead, any raksha may increase an existing Trait or gain a new one at the start of each story, provided she has the experience to afford it; Storytellers should still apply discretion when a player wants her raksha to suddenly manifest knowledge or skills she was never plausibly exposed to.
compatibility: All raksha, common and noble alike; the Heart Grace's 20-point increase to 4 additionally requires the raksha to have already spent more than 200 experience points before it becomes purchasable at all.
notes: Chapter Seven: Storytelling, the 'Fair Folk Experience' and 'Fair Folk Training Time' boxed sidebar, p. 321 (PDF 322), sitting between 'The Fair Folk and the Deathlords' and 'Others: God-Bloods and Outcastes.' This is the only genuinely player-facing, character-advancement-relevant mechanic found anywhere in Chapters One, Two, Six, or Seven during this triage pass, and it fills a real gap: every other Fair Folk row inventoried so far covers character creation or Charms, not this post-creation experience-cost/training-time framework.

name: Selective Conception
summary: Full conscious control of fertility: a female raksha can choose to conceive (or not) at will, and always knows if she has conceived. A purely physical, splat-agnostic Merit with no Exalted-specific language to adapt.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit have full conscious control of their fertility. They may be as sexually active as desired and yet as fertile as always when they decide. Females with this Merit can automatically conceive as a result of a given union for a cost of one Willpower point, and such characters automatically know if they become pregnant. Males cannot assure conception and do not know if they sire offspring, but they may withhold their fertility as desired.
compatibility: Any raksha wearing a Mote capable of procreation, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-selective-conception (Exalted Players Guide, Chapter One: Merits and Flaws). Lunar's own notes found no splat-specific eligibility language in this entry, so it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written -- a raksha's Mote is a stable body for as long as she wears it, and nothing about this Merit depends on being Exalted, having Essence, or any other trait raksha lack.

name: Ambidextrous
summary: For one point, negates offhand penalties; the two-point ("omniambidextrous") version also lets the character hold weapons/tools with their feet as readily as their hands. Raksha pay the ordinary, non-Exalted cost for either version, since the book's discount is named for Lunars specifically.
mechanics: For one point, the character can use both hands equally well and never suffers an offhand penalty for any task. Characters with the two-point version of this Merit can also hold weapons and tools with their feet as readily as their hands, an adaptation highly useful for characters who have lost the use of both hands. Matters of balance and common sense still apply, so omniambidextrous characters will not be able to walk around carrying objects with every hand and foot simultaneously.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; pays the full 2-pt. cost for the omniambidextrous version, since the discounted 1-pt. price is named for Lunar Exalted specifically and raksha are not Exalted.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-ambidextrous. Lunar's row documents a Lunar-specific discount ("Lunars pay only one point to be omniambidextrous") that does not extend to any other splat, including Fair Folk; the underlying Merit itself carries no eligibility restriction, so raksha may purchase either version at the ordinary, undiscounted cost.

name: Acute Sense
summary: One or more senses heightened to superhuman sensitivity; the 1-pt. version adds dice to Perception/Awareness rolls involving that sense but risks sensory overload, while the 3-pt. version grants preternatural acuity. A raksha's Mote-shape can carry either tier exactly as written.
mechanics: The character has one or more senses heightened to superhuman sensitivity, for a cost of one bonus point each. The character adds two dice to any Perception and/or Awareness dice pool involving a heightened sense, but his player must make a reflexive Wits + Awareness roll at standard difficulty whenever that sense experiences extremely intense stimuli; failure inflicts a one-die penalty to all actions requiring concentration until the stimulus abates. If a character instead pays three bonus points per sense, the sense is heightened to preternatural acuity. Bonus points awarded by a heightened sense do not aid in resisting sensory-overload rolls.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; stacks with, and its overload rolls are unaffected by, the Special Sense Merit below.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-acute-sense. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written, since a raksha's Mote possesses ordinary senses that can be heightened like anyone else's.

name: Double-Jointed
summary: Contortionist flexibility: the 1-pt. version adds a die to grappling/Athletics/Larceny rolls benefiting from flexibility; the 3-pt. version adds two dice and grants near-impossible feats of contortion. Raksha pay the full, non-Exalted cost for the greater version.
mechanics: For a cost of one point, the character is unusually supple and capable of remarkable feats of contortion, adding one die to grappling rolls and to Athletics or Larceny rolls where flexibility proves advantageous. Characters with the three-point version are uncanny contortionists, adding two dice to all rolls benefiting from flexibility and able to bend every finger to the wrist, lock their legs straight up, maintain indefinite splits, dislocate and reset joints painlessly and slip free of most conventional restraints with a Dexterity + Athletics roll.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; pays the full 3-pt. cost for the greater version, since the discounted 2-pt. price is named for Lunar Exalted specifically.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-double-jointed. Lunar's row documents a Lunar-specific 2-pt. discount for the greater version that does not extend to any other splat; the base Merit carries no eligibility restriction, so raksha purchase it at the ordinary, undiscounted cost.

name: Pain Tolerance
summary: Characters with this Merit can shrug off injuries that would leave most individuals unconscious or writhing in agony, at increasing tiers of pain-immunity and Awareness-roll cost. A purely physical Merit with no eligibility restriction to adapt.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit can shrug off injuries that would leave most individuals unconscious or writhing in agony. For three points, the difficulty of touch-based Awareness rolls increases by one. Five points allow the character to ignore two dice of wound penalties, at the same touch-Awareness cost; the character feels nothing and may continue acting without penalty for injuries short of actual maiming. The downside to seven-point resilience is that the character automatically fails rolls requiring a sense of touch and must visually inspect his body for injuries needing treatment. The effects of Pain Tolerance are not cumulative with Charms and other magic that negate wound penalties; only the most powerful effect applies.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; not cumulative with any Charm or shaping-combat effect that already negates wound penalties.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-pain-tolerance. Lunar's own notes found no eligibility restriction here -- only flavor text noting the Merit is common among ghosts and Abyssal deathknights -- so it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written.

name: Large Size
summary: Characters are roughly 25 percent (4-pt.) or nearly twice (6-pt.) larger than average, gaining bonus health levels but suffering a Dexterity penalty for fine manipulation at the higher tier. A raksha with this Merit keeps her extra bulk and bonus health level(s) across any shape she assumes with her Assumption-type Charms, since her Mote is a chosen form rather than a fixed body.
mechanics: Characters with the four-point version of this Merit are roughly 25 percent larger than average, standing over seven feet tall and usually weighing in at 300 or more pounds; such bulk grants one additional -0 health level. For six points, the character is almost impossibly huge, standing eight to nine feet tall and weighing 500 or more pounds, receiving one -0 level and one -1 level but losing one die from Dexterity rolls to use small weapons, writing instruments, or other tools not built for such massive hands. The added toughness is immediately evident to everyone, and the character may have to stoop through doorways built for smaller folk. A raksha with this Merit is proportionally larger in every shape she assumes and keeps the extra health level(s) in each, since a raksha's true self has no fixed body at all -- only whatever Mote or elemental shape she is currently wearing (see assumption-of-elemental-shape).
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; the size and its bonus health level(s) persist across any shape assumed via Assumption-type Charms.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-large-size, which documents this Merit's bonus health level(s) carrying into every Lunar shapechanged form (cross-referencing Prey's Skin Disguise for the one Lunar exception). Fair Folk have no Prey's Skin Disguise equivalent, but the underlying logic transfers directly: a raksha has no true form of her own, only Motes and elemental shapes assumed through the universal Assumption-type Charm tree (see assumption-of-elemental-shape), so this Merit's size and bonus health level(s) are reinterpreted here as persisting across whatever shape she is currently wearing rather than across Lunar 'forms.'

name: Legendary Attribute
summary: Grants the potential to raise a Physical (or, in other versions, Social or Mental) Attribute one dot higher than the normal cap; raksha pay the full mortal 5-pt. cost rather than the 3-pt. Exalted discount, since Fair Folk are not Exalted, but the underlying mechanic maps directly onto a raksha's own Attribute ceiling.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit have the potential to attain a rating one dot higher than the normal limit their power imposes. This may be done during character creation or after. Other versions of this Merit exist to accommodate Social and Mental Attributes, following the same rules apart from category. For a raksha, the 'normal limit' this Merit raises is her own Attribute ceiling: a noble raksha may not normally exceed 7 dots (4 added dots) in an Attribute, and a common raksha may not exceed 4 dots, without a Charm-granted mutation (see fair-folk-creation-overview-noble / fair-folk-creation-overview-common); this Merit raises that ceiling by one further dot in the chosen Attribute, exactly as the Exalted version raises an Essence-tied cap by one dot.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; pays the full mortal 5-pt. cost, since the reduced 3-pt. price is stated 'for Exalted' generically and raksha are not Exalted.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-legendary-attribute. The book's discount applies 'for Exalted' generically, which does not extend to Fair Folk; raksha pay the full mortal cost. The underlying mechanic (raising a hard Attribute cap by one dot) was reinterpreted against the raksha-specific Attribute ceilings documented in fair-folk-creation-overview-noble and -common (7 dots for nobles, 4 for commoners, both without a Charm-granted mutation) rather than the Exalted Essence-tied cap, since raksha do not use that formula.

name: Special Resistance
summary: For every point invested, adds one die to Resistance/Endurance rolls versus poison or disease, or buys immunity to a specific poison/disease. A purely physical Merit with no eligibility restriction to adapt.
mechanics: For every point invested in this Merit, the character adds one die on applicable Resistance and Endurance rolls versus poison or disease, to a maximum of five additional dice of either form of injury. Alternately, the character may have total immunity to a specific poison or disease for a cost of one point, suffering no ill effects from that toxin or malady; it is not possible to purchase immunity to infected wounds this way. All forms of this Merit assume the character has built her resistance through repeated exposure to the appropriate danger, intentionally or otherwise.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-special-resistance. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written.

name: Special Sense
summary: One or more senses that process stimuli beyond the normal ranges for the character's species (e.g. heat vision, ultrasonic hearing); no fixed mechanical effect, at Storyteller discretion, and stacks with Acute Sense.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit have one or more senses that process stimuli beyond the normal ranges for their species -- detecting heat as well as visible light, hearing high-frequency pitches, or the like. There is no fixed mechanical effect for this broader sensitivity, but Storytellers should accommodate the character's gift when narrating sensory details. If taken alongside the matching Acute Sense Merit, the character's heightened awareness also applies to the unusual range of that sense. Every significant expansion of a single sense's range costs two bonus points.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; explicitly stacks with the Acute Sense Merit.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-special-sense. Lunar's own notes found only flavor examples ('an uncapped Demesne,' 'an especially pronounced Lunar Tell') in this entry, not an eligibility restriction; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written, and a raksha's own Wyld-touched nature is at least as fitting a flavor source as either example.

name: Mutation
summary: Unusual, unnatural physical features from supernatural parentage, exposure to the Wyld, or an uncapped Demesne; useful mutations are purchased as Merits, harmful ones as Flaws, and characters with an Essence pool may fuel activation costs with motes instead of Willpower. Arguably an even more natural fit for the Fair Folk than for any Creation-born splat, since raksha are literally beings of Wyld-stuff wearing a chosen shape.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit display unusual or unnatural features, typically as a result of supernatural parentage or direct or ancestral exposure to the Wyld or an uncapped Demesne. Aberrations purchased with this Trait take the form of Wyld mutations (see Exalted, pp. 280-281, or this book's own Sword Grace Mutation Charms, such as armament-of-flesh and surpassing-excellence, for a raksha-appropriate framework). Useful mutations require bonus points equal to their mutation-point rating + 2; harmful mutations taken as Flaws grant bonus points equal to their mutation-point rating + 1. Characters with an Essence pool may spend 2 motes of Essence to fuel any activation costs required by mutations but may not purchase Feats of Willpower under any circumstances; a character with a superior natural healing rate cannot purchase the Regeneration affliction. The Storyteller may veto or modify the cost of any mutation deemed unfair, particularly if the feature is already covered by another Trait. Features obtained from this Merit do not count as actual Wyld mutations for determining whether a creature can safely endure Creation.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; a raksha's single Essence pool (permanent Essence x 10, no Personal/Peripheral split) qualifies for the mote-fueled activation-cost option exactly as written.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-flaw-mutation, which names 'an especially pronounced Lunar Tell' as one flavor source and cross-references Exalted: The Lunars' own mutation-point tables. Fair Folk have no Tell, but they have a far more direct thematic claim to Wyld mutation than any Creation-born splat -- raksha are quite literally Wyld-stuff given shape -- so the cross-reference was redirected to this book's own Sword Grace Mutation Charms (armament-of-flesh, surpassing-excellence, and the rest of that section) as the in-family framework, alongside the core Exalted mutation tables the entry also cites. The mote-fueled activation-cost clause applies directly, since raksha have an Essence pool.

name: Common Sense
summary: A decent grasp of what constitutes a good idea, a bad idea and a very bad idea; won't rush into calamity without recognizing her folly. A purely mental Merit with no eligibility restriction to adapt.
mechanics: A character with this Merit has a decent grasp of what constitutes a good idea, a bad idea and a very bad idea. She won't rush into calamity without recognizing her folly, though nothing prevents her from ignoring her better judgment. This Merit chiefly exists to warn inexperienced players about obvious dangers implicit in a course of action; the Storyteller should give fair warning in such cases without belaboring the point.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-common-sense. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written.

name: Internal Compass
summary: Uncanny sense of direction; gains one extra die to all rolls to navigate a ship or find her way through a maze. A purely mental Merit with no eligibility restriction to adapt.
mechanics: The character has an uncanny sense of direction and gains one extra die to all rolls to navigate a ship or find her way through a maze. She can orient herself with regard to the cardinal directions of Creation or the Underworld with a Wits + Awareness roll at standard difficulty.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-internal-compass. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written -- a raksha operating in Rakshastan or the Deep Wyld can orient by 'the cardinal directions of Creation' just as easily as any Exalt visiting the Wyld's borders.

name: Eidetic Recall
summary: Nearly perfect memory of everything witnessed, at a cost of one bonus point per sense the character can infallibly recall. Raksha pay the ordinary per-sense cost, since the flat discounted price is named for Alchemical Exalted specifically.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit have a nearly perfect memory of everything they have witnessed, at a cost of one bonus point for every sense the character can infallibly recall. It is assumed this record is always functioning, though the Storyteller may require a Wits + Awareness roll to memorize and remember details observed in moments of intense stress (such as combat).
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; pays the ordinary per-sense cost, since the flat 3-pt. discount for full (all five senses) recall is named for Alchemical Exalted specifically and does not extend to Fair Folk.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-eidetic-recall, which documents an Alchemical Exalted-specific flat discount. That discount is named for a different splat entirely and has no bearing on Fair Folk eligibility; raksha purchase this Merit at the ordinary, undiscounted per-sense cost, since the base Merit carries no eligibility restriction.

name: Prodigy
summary: Grants one additional Favored Ability each time purchased. The book's explicit exclusion names only Solar, Abyssal and Lunar Exalted (whose own Exalted status already imposes this cap) and Alchemical Exalted (who favor Attributes, not Abilities); Dragon-Blooded and Sidereal Exalted, whose Caste/Favored Ability structure closely parallels a raksha's own, are left eligible. Included here on that same parallel, since Fair Folk are not named in either exclusion and their Caste/Favored Ability caps work the same way as a Dragon-Blooded's or Sidereal's.
mechanics: The character excels at a particular skill or knowledge, gaining one additional Favored Ability every time this Merit is purchased. Characters may not have more than five Favored Abilities in total. For a raksha, this reinterprets as one additional Caste or Favored Ability beyond the normal limits set at character creation (5 Caste + 3 Favored for a noble, 5 Caste + 1 Favored for a commoner; see fair-folk-creation-overview-noble / -common), capped at five total Favored Abilities as in the original text. The increased aptitude lowers the experience cost to raise the Ability by 2 and adds one die to all rolls involving it; this bonus does not adjust the Trait's rating for experience-cost purposes, but it does grant superhuman mastery for characters who purchase their fifth dot.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; a judgment call, since the book neither names nor excludes Fair Folk, but the exclusion's own stated reasoning (a fixed Exalted-status ability cap) applies to Solar/Abyssal/Lunar specifically, while Dragon-Blooded and Sidereal Exalted -- whose Caste/Favored Ability caps closely resemble a raksha's own -- remain eligible.
notes: JUDGMENT CALL: Lunar's own row (pg-merit-prodigy) is disposition 'excluded' for Lunars specifically, since the book names Solars, Abyssals and Lunars by name as ineligible ('who already have these limits as part of their Exalted status'). Fair Folk are named in neither that exclusion nor the separate Alchemical exclusion (Alchemicals favor Attributes over Abilities; raksha favor Abilities via Caste/Favored Abilities, like Dragon-Blooded and Sidereals, both of whom the text leaves eligible). Since raksha use a directly analogous Caste Ability (5) / Favored Ability (1 or 3) / total-5-Favored-cap structure to Dragon-Blooded and Sidereal Exalted rather than to the excluded three, this Merit is included here as selectable by analogy rather than excluded by silence. Flagged clearly as a judgment call in case a future pass disagrees.

name: Virtue Specialty
summary: Moral fortitude strengthened under specific conditions, adding dice to Virtue rolls equal to half the points invested when a specialty circumstance is invoked. Raksha have the same four Virtues (Compassion, Conviction, Temperance, Valor) as any Exalt, so this Merit applies directly.
mechanics: A character with this Merit finds his moral resolve strengthened under certain conditions -- a meek villager standing as a lion in defense of family, a celibate ascetic better resisting temptation. The character receives additional dice to applicable Virtue rolls equal to half the points invested in this Merit, though this also increases the difficulty where the Storyteller wishes to test against his moral judgment. A character may not have more than one specialty die for a given Virtue, mirroring the restriction on Ability specialties.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; applies to any of the four Virtues -- Compassion, Conviction, Temperance, Valor -- exactly as it would for an Exalt.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-virtue-specialty. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written, since raksha use the same four Virtue Traits as every other character type in this game line.

name: Driving Passion
summary: A Nature-tied all-consuming goal that grants a bonus die whenever the character takes action directly furthering it; resolving or betraying it changes the character's Traits. Raksha choose a Nature at character creation exactly as any Exalt does, so this Merit applies unmodified.
mechanics: Characters with a Driving Passion live for a cause directly tied to their Nature (most commonly Architect or Visionary), of any scope, from liberating a nation to avenging a loved one's murder to becoming a peerless master of a craft. Whenever the character takes action directly furthering this goal, her player adds one additional die to the roll involved, with the Storyteller as final arbiter of which situations merit the bonus. If a character actually resolves or fulfills her Driving Passion, she immediately loses this Merit and gains six experience points.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-driving-passion. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written, since Step One of raksha character creation (see fair-folk-creation-overview-noble / -common) includes choosing a Nature exactly as core Exalted does.

name: Tactical Instincts
summary: Intuitive grasp of tactics: with a Wits + Lore roll, instantly discerns weaknesses/distribution of forces in a battle or game board, building a bonus pool usable to aid Wits/Presence rolls to command forces. A purely mental Merit with no eligibility restriction to adapt.
mechanics: The character has an intuitive understanding of tactics. With a Wits + Lore roll at standard difficulty, upon glancing at any contested forces or the arrangement of a game board, the character immediately discerns all weaknesses and distribution of strength. Successes accumulate as a pool of extra dice the player may subsequently apply to Lore rolls to devise a winning strategy or Presence rolls to command forces pursuing that victory (no more than three dice per roll, unused dice lost at scene's end). Characters may not reevaluate the tactical scenario to refresh their bonus pool until they use it again.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-tactical-instincts. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written, and fits Warrior-caste raksha (see warrior-caste) especially well.

name: True Love
summary: A deep and abiding romance with a partner who reciprocates; adds one die to rolls in defense of or aid of that loved one, and if the lover perishes the character may substitute this bond for Conviction to regain Willpower. Raksha have the same Conviction Virtue and Willpower Trait as any Exalt, so this Merit applies unmodified.
mechanics: A character with this Merit shares a deep and abiding romance with a partner who reciprocates that affection. This commitment adds one die to all rolls in defense or aid of that loved one. The player may also roll (Compassion + 1) in place of Conviction for her character to regain Willpower each morning, if so desired. If the character's lover perishes, she immediately loses this Merit, but may subsume her feelings into an appropriate Driving Passion, with Storyteller approval.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-true-love. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written, since raksha use the same Compassion/Conviction Virtue pair and daily Willpower-regain roll as any other character type in this game line.

name: True Paragon
summary: The character exudes formal-code honor and nobility; may spend bonus points/experience to raise Virtues above the normal 5 maximum (up to 6), and may roll her highest Virtue in place of Conviction to regain Willpower while asleep. Restricted by its own text to characters with the Paragon Nature, which raksha choose from the same Nature list as any Exalt.
mechanics: The character exudes honor and nobility, either from a formal code or an instinctive fulfillment of what she believes is right. She may spend bonus and experience points to raise any Virtue to a rating of 6 (or one point above her permitted maximum if it is otherwise raised past 5 for other reasons); this does not allow permanent Willpower to exceed 10. The player of a character with this Merit may also roll her highest Virtue in place of the standard Conviction roll to regain Willpower after sleeping. Only characters with the Paragon Nature may purchase or retain this Merit; characters who betray their code lose it without compensation.
compatibility: Any raksha with the Paragon Nature, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-true-paragon. The restriction here is by Nature (Paragon), not by Exalt type, and raksha choose a Nature during Step One of character creation (see fair-folk-creation-overview-noble / -common) exactly as core Exalted does, so this Merit applies to Fair Folk unmodified.

name: Jack of All Trades
summary: Broad basis of knowledge and skill, with an almost preternatural ability to adapt understanding to new purposes; suffers no penalty to Attribute rolls lacking the required Ability for a dice pool. A purely mental Merit with no eligibility restriction to adapt.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit have a broad basis of knowledge and skill to draw upon and an almost preternatural ability to adapt their understanding to new purposes and situations. They suffer no penalty to Attribute rolls lacking the required Ability for a dice pool.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-jack-of-all-trades. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written.

name: Born to Rule
summary: Conveys authority in every gesture and inflection; adds one die to all Social rolls when interacting with an acknowledged inferior. A purely social Merit that fits noble raksha and their Freeholds especially well.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit convey authority in every gesture and inflection, most likely as a result of aristocratic upbringing or the practice of leadership. This Merit adds one die to all Social rolls when interacting with an acknowledged inferior, as determined by the Storyteller.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; especially fitting for a noble raksha's court retinue or a Freehold's ruling caste (see freehold-background, birth-background).
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-born-to-rule. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written, and pairs naturally with the noble-raksha court/Freehold framing already documented in this family's Birth and Freehold Backgrounds.

name: Enchanting Feature
summary: A striking, attractive feature or strong presence the character can exploit to add one die to pertinent Social rolls, as decided by the Storyteller. A purely social Merit with no eligibility restriction to adapt.
mechanics: Something about the character is striking and attractive or at least conveys a strong presence -- deep eyes that seem to hold the secrets of the universe, or a voice like the basso rumble of a lion. Whenever the character can exploit this feature, he adds one die to all pertinent Social rolls, as decided by the Storyteller.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-enchanting-feature. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written.

name: Innocuous
summary: The two-point version makes the character forgettable and hard to pick out of a crowd; the four-point (Supernatural) version cloaks the character's identity from memory almost entirely. The book bars only Sidereal Exalted, whose innate Arcane Fate already supersedes it; Fair Folk are not named and remain fully eligible for either version.
mechanics: Characters with the two-point version have an eerily unremarkable visage; no one is apt to pick them from a crowd unless their coloring is dramatically different from the locals'. This anonymity adds one die to pertinent Larceny and Stealth rolls and adds one to the difficulty of any casual pursuit or investigation, though it grants no bonus if the character does something memorable (such as displaying any level of an anima banner, if applicable). Characters must have Appearance 2+ to purchase this version. The four-point version is a Supernatural Merit: witnesses' memories of the character blur even during direct interaction, requiring a Wits + Essence roll (base difficulty 6, reduced by 1 per significant event in the previous week) to recall more than superficial details; magical beings (Essence 2+) indefinitely ignore the aura once they pierce it, but only against a hidden character of lower permanent Essence. Veiled characters may not have Followers, Henchmen, a Cult, or similar fame-dependent Backgrounds, and are capped at two Contacts, Mentor, or similarly socially dependent Backgrounds.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; the 4-pt. version's Essence-based memory-piercing mechanic applies directly, since raksha have a permanent Essence rating and a single Essence pool.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-innocuous, disposition 'excluded' there only because Sidereals (a different target family) are explicitly barred by the book's own text. Fair Folk are named in no restriction here and are fully eligible for both versions; the 4-pt. version's Essence-based mechanics apply cleanly since raksha have their own permanent Essence rating and single Essence pool (see fair-folk-creation-overview-noble / -common).

name: Favor
summary: As a Merit, someone of roughly equal or greater power owes the character a favor, scaled 1-4 points by the severity/danger of the service that would repay it (2/4/6 points for minor/moderate/major favors owed by Yu-Shan's Celestial courts); as a Flaw, the character owes such a favor to someone else. A purely social Trait with no eligibility restriction to adapt.
mechanics: As a Merit, someone of roughly equal or greater power owes the character a favor. One point requires a task of a few days with no foreseen danger; two points, a service with considerable inconvenience but little danger; three points, substantial risk of injury or misfortune; four points, saving the favor holder's life or fulfilling any single demand whenever demanded. In the politics of Yu-Shan and the great spirit courts, a minor Celestial favor is worth two points, a moderate favor four, and a major favor six. Taken as a Flaw, the character instead owes such a favor to someone powerful and well-connected enough to call it in. Either way, a Favor lasts until called due, after which the Trait becomes null without further compensation. Favor debts may be transferred between parties as social currency without the original debtor's consent.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-flaw-favor. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry beyond a Yu-Shan setting flourish for the highest tier; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written, and fits a raksha's court intrigue and Freehold politics well.

name: Heirloom
summary: The character owns a piece of property more valuable than her means and lifestyle can afford, for only one bonus point regardless of the item's Resource value. A purely property Merit with no eligibility restriction to adapt.
mechanics: The character owns a piece of property more valuable than her means and lifestyle can afford -- an actual heirloom, spoils of a heist, a gift, or something more exotic still. Such an item costs only one bonus point regardless of its Resource value, though most weapons and armor purchased this way will be of exceptional quality. Because this Merit is easy to abuse, the Storyteller should probably require purchase of Resources at that level if the item is sold, and assume its wealth is concentrated in narrow holdings.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; unmodified from the Players Guide text.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-heirloom. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written, though a raksha's own instinct would be to value the item's Artifact rating (see artifact-background-fair-folk) more than a mortal Resources rating.

name: Hidden Manse
summary: The character controls a Manse forgotten to history/geomantic maps, or one shrouded by a mysterious property of its arcane nature; requires the Manse Background. Raksha cannot construct Manses but can own and attune to existing ones exactly as core Exalted can, so this Merit applies unmodified to a raksha's altered Manse Background.
requirements: Manse Background (manse-background-fair-folk).
mechanics: The character controls a Manse forgotten to history and geomantic maps, or a Manse in a public area shrouded by some mysterious property of its arcane nature. Such a hidden place of power makes an excellent base of operations or secret lair, provided the character and any trusted confidants don't compromise the location. This Merit costs one point for a hidden Demesne or two points for an actual Manse.
compatibility: Any raksha with the Manse Background; per manse-background-fair-folk, raksha can own and attune to Manses and Demesnes in Creation exactly as the standard Background allows, even though they cannot construct new ones.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-hidden-manse. No splat-specific language exists in the entry text itself, and Fair Folk's own manse-background-fair-folk row confirms raksha can own and attune to existing Manses/Demesnes in Creation (recovering Essence there as though in the Wyld) even though they cannot build new ones; this Merit's 'hidden' variant applies cleanly to such an owned Manse.

name: Heir Apparent
summary: Characters with this Merit will receive an inheritance left by their parents or another benefactor once the current owner dies (or is otherwise removed); each point invested grants two dots of Backgrounds ultimately gained, cumulative with existing Backgrounds. A purely property Merit with no eligibility restriction to adapt.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit will receive an inheritance left by a parent or other benefactor once the current owner dies or is removed. Every point invested grants two dots of Backgrounds the character will ultimately gain, though no single Background may exceed five points this way; the Storyteller may add conditions (marriage, years of service, etc.) and a die of difficulty per major condition. Background dots obtained are cumulative with existing Backgrounds and may raise a Background above four dots. Typically used for Resources-adjacent, artifact, or follower-type Backgrounds, but may include business partners, contacts, or allies with Storyteller approval.
compatibility: Any raksha, common or noble; the granted dots would most naturally land in Gossamer, Retinue, Artifact, or Style (see gossamer-background, retinue-background, artifact-background-fair-folk, style-background) rather than in Resources or Followers, which raksha do not use.
notes: Derived from Lunar's pg-merit-heir-apparent. No splat-specific language exists anywhere in this entry; it applies to Fair Folk exactly as written, but the specific Background dots it grants should be drawn from raksha's own Background list (Gossamer, Retinue, Artifact, Style, Freehold, Birth) since raksha do not use Resources or Followers at all (see followers-and-resources-excluded-fair-folk).

name: Legendary Artifact
summary: A character with this Merit has gotten hold of an artifact of world-shaking power; the book explicitly discourages Storytellers from ever allowing it, calling such artifacts "innately and grossly unfair plot devices." A purely Storyteller-discretion property Merit with no eligibility restriction to adapt.
mechanics: A character with this Merit has gotten hold of an artifact of world-shaking power, a relic on par with the Mantle of Brigid or the Eye of Autochthon. These rare and often unwisely coveted devices invariably reshape the lives of all who come into contact with them, and attract the worst ambitions of gods, demons, and Exalted (or, for a raksha, other raksha courts and Deep Wyld horrors) hungry for their power.
